sources.title: People Are Hating On Apple Music's Redesigned Black-And-White Logo - Engadget
passages: Apple Music appears to be changing its 13-year-old, iconic red "beamed eighth note" icon to a much simpler black and white version, to the consternation of a large part of the internet.
The new logo has appeared in iOS 27.2 beta 4 along with an opposite scheme (white on black) in dark mode.
"This is the worst logo change of all time," said one commenter.
"Graphics is my passion-a** logo" said our news editor.
"Apple Music, but emo," "they sucked up the charm," etc.
Some people liked it, though: "That's a great icon.
" I love it ," said the X poster who was among the first to show off the update.

extraction.body: 'Boring,' 'Generic,' 'Graphics design is my passion vibes' are a few of the kinder comments. Apple Music appears to be changing its 13-year-old, iconic red "beamed eighth note" icon to a much simpler black and white version, to the consternation of a large part of the internet. The new logo has appeared in iOS 27.2 beta 4 along with an opposite scheme (white on black) in dark mode. That follows an apparent change to the full Apple Music logo to a bolder, all-lowercase logo first seen with the launch of Apple Music Hall, the company's new venue in London. Along with wiping out the color, the new logo is tilted slightly more to the left, the bottom of the notes are more oval-shaped and there's a very subtle drop shadow under the bar and notes. Apple also has a "Clear" version, and as with other icons, you can tint it to any color . Along with the icon change, Apple also removed the red color from the home screen widgets and changed the pink/red tint inside the app to blue. Default, Dark, Clear, Tinted pic.twitter.com/bg4tFTHMCe Apple has a rich history of riling up users by changing its icons and entire UI, though people usually get used to the changes and then scoff at the previous design. Still, the Music icon change appears to have struck a wrong chord (sorry) with users, who mainly found it dull and unnecessary, as Cult of Mac reported. "This is the worst logo change of all time," said one commenter. "Graphics is my passion-a** logo" said our news editor. Others were in the same vein. "Apple Music, but emo," "they sucked up the charm," etc. Some people liked it, though: "That's a great icon. That red made no sense to me," said one. " I love it ," said the X poster who was among the first to show off the update. Personally, design and icon changes always leave me confused for awhile, as if someone put all my dishes into a different cupboard. Logo and design buffs will no doubt have their say, but so far, this update seems to have more critics than fans. The app is still in beta so Apple could still change its mind, but the company usually sticks to its guns on such changes.

sources.body: Following the appearance of a redesigned wordmark in a video and an updated app icon in an iOS 27.2 beta, Apple introduced the new “identity” for Apple Music today. Apple is officially launching a rebrand of Apple Music.

extraction.body: Apple is officially launching a rebrand of Apple Music. Following the appearance of a redesigned wordmark in a video and an updated app icon in an iOS 27.2 beta, Apple introduced the new “identity” for Apple Music today. There’s a new logo, the updated wordmark, and a new sound composed by British producer Fred Again and Nest Acoustics. In a video, Apple says that for the rebrand, the company “wanted sound to create the visuals,” showing the music note logo and the wordmark underwater and how that water responded to sound. It’s a pretty cool video, honestly, and I like seeing how the water morphs the logo and wordmark. The video is also one of the most Apple things I’ve ever seen, but I still think it’s cool. The new look is expected to roll out across platforms “this week,” according to Wallpaper. I’m guessing that means it will show up in the final iOS 27.2 release, following the release candidate version of the update that launched this week.

sources.title: Apple Music’s new visual identity ripples into view – with help from Fred Again.. - Wallpaper*
passages: Apple Music has enlisted British producer Fred Again.. to help turn sound into something tangible for its new visual identity.
Built around the idea of being ‘made by sound’, the redesign takes an experimental approach, using musical frequencies to create rippling, liquid forms.
The results were achieved by playing music into a shallow bath of mineral oil and filming the resulting vibrations.
Fred Again.. and his collaborator Nest Acoustics developed a short musical composition that doubles as the brand's new sonic signature.
Individual notes were played through a transducer, a device that converts audio signals into physical vibrations, causing the oil to ripple in response.
The movements and refractions were captured on camera, providing the raw material for the new design.
The redesign includes Apple Music's typography.
A new wordmark pairs the recognisable Apple symbol with a customised version of Apple's own typeface, SF Pro.
Bold, lowercase lettering gives the service a youthful energy, while a reworked musical note icon takes its shape from the forms captured during filming.

A closer look at the people and places shaping design, from inspiring interiors to exceptional products, in an expert edit by Wallpaper* global design director Hugo Macdonald.

facts.text: Apple Music has officially launched its rebrand with a new design, logo, and more.
And in a video detailing the rebrand, Apple reveals the new look was actually “made by sound.”
Like it did when Apple TV rebranded, Apple has published a behind-the-scenes video explaining that the new logo was created practically.
We’ve seen signs for weeks that Apple Music had a big rebrand coming, including a fresh app icon and other design updates in iOS 27.2.
A story of music, collaboration and craft with Fred again.. and NEST Acoustics.
Discover how sound brought the Apple Music logo to life, captured entirely in camera.
What do you think of Apple Music’s new look? Let us know in the comments.
Check out 9to5Mac on YouTube for more Apple news:
Apple Music appears to be changing its 13-year-old, iconic red "beamed eighth note" icon to a much simpler black and white version, to the consternation of a large part of the internet.
The new logo has appeared in iOS 27.2 beta 4 along with an opposite scheme (white on black) in dark mode.
"This is the worst logo change of all time," said one commenter.
"Graphics is my passion-a** logo" said our news editor.
"Apple Music, but emo," "they sucked up the charm," etc.
Some people liked it, though: "That's a great icon.
" I love it ," said the X poster who was among the first to show off the update.
Following the appearance of a redesigned wordmark in a video and an updated app icon in an iOS 27.2 beta, Apple introduced the new “identity” for Apple Music today.
Apple is officially launching a rebrand of Apple Music.
Apple Music has enlisted British producer Fred Again.. to help turn sound into something tangible for its new visual identity.
Built around the idea of being ‘made by sound’, the redesign takes an experimental approach, using musical frequencies to create rippling, liquid forms.
The results were achieved by playing music into a shallow bath of mineral oil and filming the resulting vibrations.
Fred Again.. and his collaborator Nest Acoustics developed a short musical composition that doubles as the brand's new sonic signature.
Individual notes were played through a transducer, a device that converts audio signals into physical vibrations, causing the oil to ripple in response.
The movements and refractions were captured on camera, providing the raw material for the new design.
The redesign includes Apple Music's typography.
A new wordmark pairs the recognisable Apple symbol with a customised version of Apple's own typeface, SF Pro.
Bold, lowercase lettering gives the service a youthful energy, while a reworked musical note icon takes its shape from the forms captured during filming.

extraction.body: 'Boring,' 'Generic,' 'Graphics design is my passion vibes' are a few of the kinder comments. Apple Music appears to be changing its 13-year-old, iconic red "beamed eighth note" icon to a much simpler black and white version, to the consternation of a large part of the internet. The new logo has appeared in iOS 27.2 beta 4 along with an opposite scheme (white on black) in dark mode. That follows an apparent change to the full Apple Music logo to a bolder, all-lowercase logo first seen with the launch of Apple Music Hall, the company's new venue in London. Along with wiping out the color, the new logo is tilted slightly more to the left, the bottom of the notes are more oval-shaped and there's a very subtle drop shadow under the bar and notes. Apple also has a "Clear" version, and as with other icons, you can tint it to any color . Along with the icon change, Apple also removed the red color from the home screen widgets and changed the pink/red tint inside the app to blue. Default, Dark, Clear, Tinted pic.twitter.com/bg4tFTHMCe Apple has a rich history of riling up users by changing its icons and entire UI, though people usually get used to the changes and then scoff at the previous design. Still, the Music icon change appears to have struck a wrong chord (sorry) with users, who mainly found it dull and unnecessary, as Cult of Mac reported. "This is the worst logo change of all time," said one commenter. "Graphics is my passion-a** logo" said our news editor. Others were in the same vein. "Apple Music, but emo," "they sucked up the charm," etc. Some people liked it, though: "That's a great icon. That red made no sense to me," said one. " I love it ," said the X poster who was among the first to show off the update. Personally, design and icon changes always leave me confused for awhile, as if someone put all my dishes into a different cupboard. Logo and design buffs will no doubt have their say, but so far, this update seems to have more critics than fans. The app is still in beta so Apple could still change its mind, but the company usually sticks to its guns on such changes.

extraction.body: Apple is officially launching a rebrand of Apple Music. Following the appearance of a redesigned wordmark in a video and an updated app icon in an iOS 27.2 beta, Apple introduced the new “identity” for Apple Music today. There’s a new logo, the updated wordmark, and a new sound composed by British producer Fred Again and Nest Acoustics. In a video, Apple says that for the rebrand, the company “wanted sound to create the visuals,” showing the music note logo and the wordmark underwater and how that water responded to sound. It’s a pretty cool video, honestly, and I like seeing how the water morphs the logo and wordmark. The video is also one of the most Apple things I’ve ever seen, but I still think it’s cool. The new look is expected to roll out across platforms “this week,” according to Wallpaper. I’m guessing that means it will show up in the final iOS 27.2 release, following the release candidate version of the update that launched this week.

sources.title: Google’s more personalized Gemini AI is heading to your car
passages: Google is bringing Personal Intelligence to Gemini AI in your car.

extraction.body: Google is bringing Personal Intelligence to Gemini AI in your car. With this update, Gemini in Android Auto and cars with Google built-in can tap into your information across Google apps, including Gmail, Calendar, Maps, Photos, YouTube, and Search. As an example, Google says you can ask Gemini about your flight status if you’re driving to the airport. The AI assistant can pull your flight details from a confirmation message in Gmail and then use that information to look up the status. You can also ask Gemini to “take me to my doctor’s appointment” instead of pulling up directions manually, or ask it to “find the car wash from the photo I took last week and navigate there.” [Video: Personal Intelligence in cars] Google brought its Gemini assistant to Android Auto last year before rolling it out to cars with Google built-in in April. Several carmakers—including Ford, GM, Honda, Nissan, Volvo, and Polestar—have shipped newer cars with Google built-in, which adds support for native Android apps. Google says it will connect your apps to Gemini only if you enable its Personal Intelligence setting. It will also share personalized responses only if you have your phone connected to your car. “If you don’t use Personal Intelligence, everything in the car still works: You can use navigation, listen to music, make calls, and ask questions, but the answers won’t be tailored to you,” Google says. Personal Intelligence is rolling out to Android Auto today, with support coming to cars with Google built-in in the coming months.

The AI assistant can pull your flight details from a confirmation message in Gmail and then use that information to look up the status.

You can also ask Gemini to “take me to my doctor’s appointment” instead of pulling up directions manually, or ask it to “find the car wash from the photo I took last week and navigate there.” [Video: Personal Intelligence in cars] Google brought its Gemini assistant to Android Auto last year before rolling it out to cars with Google built-in in April.
Several carmakers—including Ford, GM, Honda, Nissan, Volvo, and Polestar—have shipped newer cars with Google built-in, which adds support for native Android apps.
Google says it will connect your apps to Gemini only if you enable its Personal Intelligence setting.
It will also share personalized responses only if you have your phone connected to your car.

“If you don’t use Personal Intelligence, everything in the car still works: You can use navigation, listen to music, make calls, and ask questions, but the answers won’t be tailored to you,” Google says.
Personal Intelligence is rolling out to Android Auto today, with support coming to cars with Google built-in in the coming months.

sources.title: Google is bringing a more personal version of its Gemini AI assistant to your car
passages: Google is making the Gemini AI assistant that’s already in millions of cars, trucks, and SUVs a lot more personal — a move that could push consumers even deeper into the company’s ecosystem of products.
Google said the feature will allow users to make complex requests using natural language.
Gemini will give the user answers to both questions at the same time, the company said.

Google said it will roll out “Personal Intelligence with Gemini” to vehicles in two ways — through Android Auto, an app that runs on the user’s phone and wirelessly communicates with and projects navigation, media, and messaging to the vehicle’s infotainment system, and Google Built-in , software and services that have been directly integrated into the vehicle.
Google initially launched Gemini last November in Android Auto.
That level of emmeshing might make consumers uncomfortable, although Google says users do retain full control over their data with Personal Intelligence.
This latest upgrade would connect the dots — as Google put it in its blog post — across users’ Google apps.

The company said Tuesday it’s upgrading Gemini in vehicles with a personal intelligence feature that can draw on information from Gmail, Google Calendar, YouTube, Maps, Google Search history, and other connected Google services to understand your preferences, activities, and past experiences. Google said it will roll out “Personal Intelligence with Gemini” to vehicles in two ways — through Android Auto, an app that runs on the user’s phone and wirelessly communicates with and projects navigation, media, and messaging to the vehicle’s infotainment system, and Google Built-in , software and services that have been directly integrated into the vehicle. The feature will launch in Android Auto, starting today, and expand to cars with Google Built-in in the coming months. Google initially launched Gemini last November in Android Auto. Meanwhile, Gemini’s “Personal Intelligence” feature rolled out across the U.S. in March and is now in beta in global markets. This latest upgrade would connect the dots — as Google put it in its blog post — across users’ Google apps. Drivers will have to opt in for Personalized Intelligence to work. Once a user does so, they should expect all sorts of cross-pollination. For instance, a driver who is navigating to the airport may be alerted that the flight on their calendar is delayed. Google said the feature will allow users to make complex requests using natural language. Returning to that airport example, a user might ask the AI assistant for their flight gate before quickly following up with a question about whether it’s still on time. Gemini will give the user answers to both questions at the same time, the company said. That level of emmeshing might make consumers uncomfortable, although Google says users do retain full control over their data with Personal Intelligence. The feature can be turned on or off at any time, and users can selectively choose which apps they’d like to connect, Google said. For the uninitiated, Gemini Live is a natural way to interact with an AI chatbot. Instead of typing questions, you can speak with the assistant in real time, share the camera or screen, and receive spoken responses. The feature is part of Gemini, Google’s AI assistant. The company now appears to be improving the feature with deeper personalization.

While digging through the Google app for Android (version 17.9.50.sa.arm64), folks over at Android Authority have discovered a couple of strings in the code. The first reads, “Try a version of Gemini Live that uses your personal context.” Another string says, “Try a version of Gemini Live that uses past conversations and your connected apps to provide more personalized responses.”

The publication believes the mention of “personal context” refers to Personal Intelligence. In January this year, Google brought Personal Intelligence to its Gemini to make the AI assistant more helpful in day-to-day tasks. The feature allows Gemini to analyze information from apps like Gmail, Google Photos, Google Calendar, and Google Drive. As such, the assistant can deliver answers based on personal activity, such as finding your car model from an email and checking details from a receipt.

With this update, Gemini in Android Auto and cars with Google built-in can tap into your information across Google apps, including Gmail, Calendar, Maps, Photos, YouTube, and Search.
As an example, Google says you can ask Gemini about your flight status if you’re driving to the airport.

COSTA MESA, Calif., September 23, 2026 --( BUSINESS WIRE )--Today, Experian, the global data and technology company, and Google announced a strategic collaboration that makes Experian the first personal finance app integrated with Google Gemini, expanding Experian's reach to one of the world's largest AI platforms and creating a new way for consumers to discover, access, and engage with Experian through conversational AI.

By bringing consumer-permissioned Experian credit insights into Gemini, we can help consumers better understand their credit and put their own information to work for them, in addition to the products, services, and experiences we power directly for our clients."
Connecting to Google Gemini's Connect App ecosystem is designed to be simple, secure, and consumer controlled.
Users sign in to their Google account and open Gemini.
From the Personal Intelligence menu, they can navigate to Connected Apps, select Experian, and choose to link and authorize access to their Experian account.
After securely authenticating, consumers can ask Gemini questions about their Experian credit information, including their FICO® credit rating and the key factors influencing it.
Consumers can manage their connected app settings through Google's Personal Intelligence settings at any time.

As AI assistants increasingly become part of how people navigate everyday decisions, Experian is extending trusted financial information into an emerging consumer channel while keeping consumers in control of whether their Experian information is connected and used.

The collaboration also creates a new point of discovery for Experian, allowing consumers already using Gemini to connect with Experian, where they can access a broader range of financial products, services, and capabilities through the Experian app or website.

The Gemini integration gives Experian another way to reach consumers, both existing members and people discovering Experian for the first time, through an AI platform that is increasingly part of consumers' everyday lives.

Gemini becomes another channel in Experian's broader consumer ecosystem, complementing the products and services it provides directly and the experiences it powers for financial institutions and other clients.
Existing Experian members can connect their accounts, while consumers who discover Experian through Gemini can join Experian at no cost.

Google is making the Gemini AI assistant that’s already in millions of cars, trucks, and SUVs a lot more personal — a move that could push consumers even deeper into the company’s ecosystem of products.
Google said the feature will allow users to make complex requests using natural language.
Gemini will give the user answers to both questions at the same time, the company said.

Google said it will roll out “Personal Intelligence with Gemini” to vehicles in two ways — through Android Auto, an app that runs on the user’s phone and wirelessly communicates with and projects navigation, media, and messaging to the vehicle’s infotainment system, and Google Built-in , software and services that have been directly integrated into the vehicle.
Google initially launched Gemini last November in Android Auto.
That level of emmeshing might make consumers uncomfortable, although Google says users do retain full control over their data with Personal Intelligence.
This latest upgrade would connect the dots — as Google put it in its blog post — across users’ Google apps.

extraction.body: Google is bringing Personal Intelligence to Gemini AI in your car. With this update, Gemini in Android Auto and cars with Google built-in can tap into your information across Google apps, including Gmail, Calendar, Maps, Photos, YouTube, and Search. As an example, Google says you can ask Gemini about your flight status if you’re driving to the airport. The AI assistant can pull your flight details from a confirmation message in Gmail and then use that information to look up the status. You can also ask Gemini to “take me to my doctor’s appointment” instead of pulling up directions manually, or ask it to “find the car wash from the photo I took last week and navigate there.” [Video: Personal Intelligence in cars] Google brought its Gemini assistant to Android Auto last year before rolling it out to cars with Google built-in in April. Several carmakers—including Ford, GM, Honda, Nissan, Volvo, and Polestar—have shipped newer cars with Google built-in, which adds support for native Android apps. Google says it will connect your apps to Gemini only if you enable its Personal Intelligence setting. It will also share personalized responses only if you have your phone connected to your car. “If you don’t use Personal Intelligence, everything in the car still works: You can use navigation, listen to music, make calls, and ask questions, but the answers won’t be tailored to you,” Google says. Personal Intelligence is rolling out to Android Auto today, with support coming to cars with Google built-in in the coming months.

By bringing consumer-permissioned Experian credit insights into Gemini, we can help consumers better understand their credit and put their own information to work for them, in addition to the products, services, and experiences we power directly for our clients."
Connecting to Google Gemini's Connect App ecosystem is designed to be simple, secure, and consumer controlled.
Users sign in to their Google account and open Gemini.
From the Personal Intelligence menu, they can navigate to Connected Apps, select Experian, and choose to link and authorize access to their Experian account.
After securely authenticating, consumers can ask Gemini questions about their Experian credit information, including their FICO® credit rating and the key factors influencing it.
Consumers can manage their connected app settings through Google's Personal Intelligence settings at any time.

As AI assistants increasingly become part of how people navigate everyday decisions, Experian is extending trusted financial information into an emerging consumer channel while keeping consumers in control of whether their Experian information is connected and used.

The collaboration also creates a new point of discovery for Experian, allowing consumers already using Gemini to connect with Experian, where they can access a broader range of financial products, services, and capabilities through the Experian app or website.

The Gemini integration gives Experian another way to reach consumers, both existing members and people discovering Experian for the first time, through an AI platform that is increasingly part of consumers' everyday lives.

Gemini becomes another channel in Experian's broader consumer ecosystem, complementing the products and services it provides directly and the experiences it powers for financial institutions and other clients.
Existing Experian members can connect their accounts, while consumers who discover Experian through Gemini can join Experian at no cost.

COSTA MESA, Calif., September 23, 2026 --( BUSINESS WIRE )--Today, Experian, the global data and technology company, and Google announced a strategic collaboration that makes Experian the first personal finance app integrated with Google Gemini, expanding Experian's reach to one of the world's largest AI platforms and creating a new way for consumers to discover, access, and engage with Experian through conversational AI. Existing Experian members can connect their accounts, while consumers who discover Experian through Gemini can join Experian at no cost. As AI assistants increasingly become part of how people navigate everyday decisions, Experian is extending trusted financial information into an emerging consumer channel while keeping consumers in control of whether their Experian information is connected and used. The collaboration also creates a new point of discovery for Experian, allowing consumers already using Gemini to connect with Experian, where they can access a broader range of financial products, services, and capabilities through the Experian app or website. Turning Credit Information into Understanding Consumers can ask Gemini questions about their Experian credit information and receive personalized responses designed to make that information easier to understand. For example, a user can ask, "@Experian, what's my credit rating?" and be prompted to connect directly with Experian to receive their credit rating within the Gemini experience. They can also ask about key factors influencing their credit, giving them additional context about where they stand and what may be affecting their credit profile. Rather than simply viewing static information, consumers can ask questions in a conversational experience that combines Experian's trusted credit data with Gemini's AI capabilities to help make credit information easier to understand. Consumers who want to view their FICO® Score 8i will continue to access it directly through the Experian website or app, where they can access a broader range of products, services, and capabilities designed to help them manage their financial lives and find more ways to save time and money. Users also have the ability to tag "@Experian" to connect with the Experian app within a chat when asking a credit-related question. Existing Experian members can authorize access to their Experian account, while consumers who are new to Experian can join at no cost and establish an Experian membership. After securely authenticating, consumers can ask Gemini questions about their Experian credit information, including their FICO® credit rating and the key factors influencing it. Consumers can manage their connected app settings through Google's Personal Intelligence settings at any time. Expanding How Consumers Discover and Access Experian The collaboration builds on Experian's long track record of consumer innovation and advances its strategy of giving consumers more ways to engage where they choose. As consumers increasingly use AI-powered assistants alongside apps, websites, and other digital experiences, Experian is expanding the ways consumers can access and engage with trusted financial information. Gemini becomes another channel in Experian's broader consumer ecosystem, complementing the products and services it provides directly and the experiences it powers for financial institutions and other clients. Together, these experiences give consumers more ways to access Experian information, insights, and capabilities throughout their financial lives. The companies also plan to build on the collaboration over time, expanding the Experian capabilities consumers can access through Gemini—such as subscription cancellation, which could help consumers save on unwanted subscriptions they currently pay for. sources.title: Google is bringing a more personal version of its Gemini AI assistant to your car
passages: Google is making the Gemini AI assistant that’s already in millions of cars, trucks, and SUVs a lot more personal — a move that could push consumers even deeper into the company’s ecosystem of products.
Google said the feature will allow users to make complex requests using natural language.
Gemini will give the user answers to both questions at the same time, the company said.

Google said it will roll out “Personal Intelligence with Gemini” to vehicles in two ways — through Android Auto, an app that runs on the user’s phone and wirelessly communicates with and projects navigation, media, and messaging to the vehicle’s infotainment system, and Google Built-in , software and services that have been directly integrated into the vehicle.
Google initially launched Gemini last November in Android Auto.
That level of emmeshing might make consumers uncomfortable, although Google says users do retain full control over their data with Personal Intelligence.
This latest upgrade would connect the dots — as Google put it in its blog post — across users’ Google apps.

extraction.body: Google is making the Gemini AI assistant that’s already in millions of cars, trucks, and SUVs a lot more personal — a move that could push consumers even deeper into the company’s ecosystem of products. The company said Tuesday it’s upgrading Gemini in vehicles with a personal intelligence feature that can draw on information from Gmail, Google Calendar, YouTube, Maps, Google Search history, and other connected Google services to understand your preferences, activities, and past experiences. Google said it will roll out “Personal Intelligence with Gemini” to vehicles in two ways — through Android Auto, an app that runs on the user’s phone and wirelessly communicates with and projects navigation, media, and messaging to the vehicle’s infotainment system, and Google Built-in , software and services that have been directly integrated into the vehicle. The feature will launch in Android Auto, starting today, and expand to cars with Google Built-in in the coming months. Google initially launched Gemini last November in Android Auto. Meanwhile, Gemini’s “Personal Intelligence” feature rolled out across the U.S. in March and is now in beta in global markets. This latest upgrade would connect the dots — as Google put it in its blog post — across users’ Google apps. Drivers will have to opt in for Personalized Intelligence to work. Once a user does so, they should expect all sorts of cross-pollination. For instance, a driver who is navigating to the airport may be alerted that the flight on their calendar is delayed. Google said the feature will allow users to make complex requests using natural language. Returning to that airport example, a user might ask the AI assistant for their flight gate before quickly following up with a question about whether it’s still on time. Gemini will give the user answers to both questions at the same time, the company said. That level of emmeshing might make consumers uncomfortable, although Google says users do retain full control over their data with Personal Intelligence. The feature can be turned on or off at any time, and users can selectively choose which apps they’d like to connect, Google said. sources.title: Google May Bring Personal Intelligence to Gemini Live - SammyGuru
passages: While digging through the Google app for Android (version 17.9.50.sa.arm64), folks over at Android Authority have discovered a couple of strings in the code.

The first reads, “Try a version of Gemini Live that uses your personal context.” Another string says, “Try a version of Gemini Live that uses past conversations and your connected apps to provide more personalized responses.”
Google appears to make its AI assistant more personal and useful.
A fresh report suggests that Gemini Live could soon support a feature called Personal Intelligence.
This could allow the AI to use information from a user’s Google apps to offer more relevant answers.
The same capability now appears to be coming to Gemini Live, though the exact timeline remains unclear.
Google may initially restrict access to paid subscribers of its AI plans, such as AI Pro and AI Ultra.
Eventually, it should become available to free users.
For the uninitiated, Gemini Live is a natural way to interact with an AI chatbot.
Instead of typing questions, you can speak with the assistant in real time, share the camera or screen, and receive spoken responses.
The feature is part of Gemini, Google’s AI assistant.
The feature allows Gemini to analyze information from apps like Gmail, Google Photos, Google Calendar, and Google Drive.
As such, the assistant can deliver answers based on personal activity, such as finding your car model from an email and checking details from a receipt.

sources.title: Blink brings 4K to its low-cost security camera lineup
passages: Amazon is launching a new lineup of Blink security cameras, including its first 4K, pan-tilt models, and battery-powered spotlight models.
There’s also the $79.99 Blink Mini 4K Plus, Blink’s first camera to support 4K resolution.

These new additions provide better resolution and extended range for monitoring your property compared to Blink’s current Mini 2K, Mini 2K Plus, and Outdoor 2K Plus offerings, with a variety of different specializations to best suit your security requirements.
Blink hasn’t specified when the cameras will start shipping, so we’ve asked for clarification and will update if we hear back.
One of the standouts is the $199.99 Blink Frontier XR Plus, a trail camera that’s designed for expansive properties that would typically require multiple cameras or specialized monitoring equipment.

It can cover up to 7,000 feet with a clear line of sight, making this Blink’s farthest-reaching camera to date. There’s also the $79.99 Blink Mini 4K Plus, Blink’s first camera to support 4K resolution. The $109.99 Spotlight Cam 2K Plus and $49.99 Mini Pan-Tilt 2K Plus are also included in the launch, as Blink’s first battery-powered spotlight and pan-tilt cameras respectively. The Mini Pan-Tilt 2K Plus is the most affordable offering in the new lineup, providing 350-degrees of pan and 115-degrees of tilt alongside night vision, two-way audio, and motion detection for people and vehicles to track where the action is happening. The $149.99 Blink Outdoor 2K XR Plus rounds out the collection. Eligible features like video descriptions, motion-activated notifications, and 60 days of cloud video storage are available as an optional subscription that starts at $3.99 per month, or you can otherwise record locally on a Blink Sync Module. All five cameras are available for preorder starting today in the US, though availability in other regions will vary by model. Blink hasn’t specified when the cameras will start shipping, so we’ve asked for clarification and will update if we hear back.

Amazon has just launched five new products as part of its Blink security camera lineup, expanding their resolution, adding a spotlight, and jazzing up their hardware format. The Blink Mini 4K+, priced at $79.99, is the company’s first 4K security camera that now goes all the way up to 4K video capture quality and offers a 115-degree horizontal field of view. The build is IP65-rated, and it also gets dual-band Wi-Fi 6 support for better network coverage. For users who pay for the accompanying subscription service, they also get access to two-way audio, AI-generated event summaries, and Smart Alerts with person and vehicle detection. Next in line is the Blink Spotlight Cam 2K+, which is the company’s first battery-powered spotlight camera. Amazon says that the spotlight kicks into action as soon as it detects motion, while video resolution is capped at 2K. This one is priced at $109.99 for buyers in the US. The Blink Mini Pan-Tilt 2K+ is the brand’s first pan-tilt-zoom camera, suited for both indoors and outdoors, complete with night vision and two-way audio support. Priced at $49.99, it offers a 350-degree pan and a 115-degree tilt range. And just like its Spotlight-series sibling, it also enables person and vehicle motion detection with a subscription. For long-range coverage, the company has introduced the Blink Outdoor 2K XR+ priced at $149.99, alongside the Blink Frontier XR+ camera, which costs $199.99 in the US. The former captures videos at up to 2K resolution with a 115-degree field of view and can cover a distance of up to 2,700 feet within a straight line of sight. The latter, according to Blink, is its farthest-reaching camera yet. When paired with the Sync Module XR+, it offers a line-of-sight coverage of up to 7,000 feet. All five of Blink’s new cameras are now up for pre-order for buyers in the US, and a bunch of other markets as well. Apple’s first HomeView hasn't reached customers yet, but the company is reportedly working on a more ambitious version. According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, Apple is developing a higher-end model with a roughly 9-inch display mounted on a robotic arm that can rotate a full 360 degrees. The current $299 HomeView is still on preorder, with deliveries beginning November 13. It uses a fixed 7-inch display on a speaker base, and Apple also sells a wall-mounted version. The idea was to bring its tight integration into the living room, kitchen, and practically every other corner of your house. Among these new gadgets was the Apple HomeView, the company's long-awaited smart home display, unveiled during its October 13 Welcome Home event. It combines a 7-inch touchscreen, built-in speakers, Apple's new conversational Siri AI, and a centralized dashboard for managing everything from security cameras to smart lighting. I was genuinely excited when Apple announced the HomeView. A 7-inch smart display from Apple sounded like something I would happily put on my kitchen counter. Eligible features like video descriptions, motion-activated notifications, and 60 days of cloud video storage are available as an optional subscription that starts at $3.99 per month, or you can otherwise record locally on a Blink Sync Module. All five cameras are available for preorder starting today in the US, though availability in other regions will vary by model. Blink hasn’t specified when the cameras will start shipping, so we’ve asked for clarification and will update if we hear back.

Amazon has just launched five new products as part of its Blink security camera lineup, expanding their resolution, adding a spotlight, and jazzing up their hardware format. The Blink Mini 4K+, priced at $79.99, is the company’s first 4K security camera that now goes all the way up to 4K video capture quality and offers a 115-degree horizontal field of view. The build is IP65-rated, and it also gets dual-band Wi-Fi 6 support for better network coverage. For users who pay for the accompanying subscription service, they also get access to two-way audio, AI-generated event summaries, and Smart Alerts with person and vehicle detection. Next in line is the Blink Spotlight Cam 2K+, which is the company’s first battery-powered spotlight camera. Amazon says that the spotlight kicks into action as soon as it detects motion, while video resolution is capped at 2K. This one is priced at $109.99 for buyers in the US. The Blink Mini Pan-Tilt 2K+ is the brand’s first pan-tilt-zoom camera, suited for both indoors and outdoors, complete with night vision and two-way audio support. Priced at $49.99, it offers a 350-degree pan and a 115-degree tilt range. And just like its Spotlight-series sibling, it also enables person and vehicle motion detection with a subscription. For long-range coverage, the company has introduced the Blink Outdoor 2K XR+ priced at $149.99, alongside the Blink Frontier XR+ camera, which costs $199.99 in the US. The former captures videos at up to 2K resolution with a 115-degree field of view and can cover a distance of up to 2,700 feet within a straight line of sight. The latter, according to Blink, is its farthest-reaching camera yet. When paired with the Sync Module XR+, it offers a line-of-sight coverage of up to 7,000 feet. All five of Blink’s new cameras are now up for pre-order for buyers in the US, and a bunch of other markets as well. Apple’s first HomeView hasn't reached customers yet, but the company is reportedly working on a more ambitious version. According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, Apple is developing a higher-end model with a roughly 9-inch display mounted on a robotic arm that can rotate a full 360 degrees. The current $299 HomeView is still on preorder, with deliveries beginning November 13. It uses a fixed 7-inch display on a speaker base, and Apple also sells a wall-mounted version. During the Welcome Home event, Apple announced a bunch of products that expand its smart home lineup. These share a connected ecosystem around the iPhone, iPad, and Mac. The idea was to bring its tight integration into the living room, kitchen, and practically every other corner of your house. Among these new gadgets was the Apple HomeView, the company's long-awaited smart home display, unveiled during its October 13 Welcome Home event. It combines a 7-inch touchscreen, built-in speakers, Apple's new conversational Siri AI, and a centralized dashboard for managing everything from security cameras to smart lighting. I was genuinely excited when Apple announced the HomeView. A 7-inch smart display from Apple sounded like something I would happily put on my kitchen counter. Then Apple published its repair prices, and my excitement took a nosedive. Why does a repair cost almost as much as a new one? Head below to get the rundown on what each brings to your home. With larger properties providing more of a challenge to manage, especially at key points like gates, pastures, outbuildings, or even at remote job sites – this camera helps to extend your visibility to keep an eye on areas that you otherwise would struggle to monitor. Unlike the above trail camera, this one offers up to 2,700 feet of total reach with unobstructed view to the hub, or up to 800 feet of reach with some trees or structures between them. This is especially handy for folks with larger yards, longer driveways, detached garages and other structures around the property, or to manage multiple entry points, too. The camera itself provides 1080p video resolution at max range settings, giving you a 115-degree field of view that broadly covers more of the surroundings alongside adding versatile range connection. Speaking of subscriptions, those who join said plan not only gain those above features, but also AI-generated summaries of the camera activity so you can quickly and easily understand what has taken place in front of the camera without needing to watch everything in full. Heading back outside, but this time focusing on providing more visibility despite the time of day/night, the Spotlight Cam 2K+ that is the Blink’s “first battery-powered spotlight camera.” It combines 2K video with built-in illumination so that you can see more around your home after the sun has set. This is a a wireless model that can be placed anywhere you want additional visibility, like above the garage, near a back gate, in a side yard, and more. Once the camera picks up on any motion, the spotlight activates and gives you a clearer view while also acting as a deterrent to unwelcome guests. sources.title: Google Maps' Gemini integration will make hands-free navigation more conversational - Engadget
passages: Google has been replacing Assistant with Gemini across all its apps, and Maps is the latest one getting an upgrade.
The AI assistant will let you interact with the app using natural conversation while you navigate the roads hands-free.

You can, for instance, ask it: "Is there a budget-friendly Japanese restaurant along my route within a couple of miles?" And after it has responded, you can keep on asking it follow-up questions, such as if a specific restaurant has a parking space and what dishes are popular there.
Once you've decided on a place, you can simply tell Gemini: "Okay, let's go there," to start navigating to it.
You'll also be able to ask Gemini to do random tasks while it's navigating and without leaving the Maps app, such as adding events to your Calendar if you allow it to connect to the app.
It's also coming to Android Auto in the future .
You can now get directions that mention landmarks that are easy to spot.
Instead of saying "turn left in 500 feet," for example, Gemini will say "turn left after the Thai Siam Restaurant." The landmark will also be highlighted in Maps as a visual cue.
This feature is now rolling out to both Android and iOS devices.
Maps will now proactively notify you of road disruptions on Android, as well, even if you're not actively navigating.
The update is rolling out over the coming weeks everywhere Gemini is available.

sources.title: Conversational Gemini navigation comes to Apple CarPlay
passages: After introducing its Gemini AI assistant to Android Auto last year, Google is now bringing it to Apple CarPlay users.
The conversational Gemini in navigation is available today for US drivers, with “rollout happening globally too,” according to Google (we’ve asked for specific regional availability details).
Google describes this CarPlay support update as a conversational way to report traffic disruptions and find information about stops and places on-the-go.

extraction.body: After introducing its Gemini AI assistant to Android Auto last year, Google is now bringing it to Apple CarPlay users. The conversational Gemini in navigation is available today for US drivers, with “rollout happening globally too,” according to Google (we’ve asked for specific regional availability details). It’s taken almost 12 months for Google to bring this to CarPlay users, but now they can talk to the voice assistant in Google Maps to get some hands-free help while driving. Users can activate the feature by tapping the Gemini icon in Google Maps on their Car’s infotainment display. Google describes this CarPlay support update as a conversational way to report traffic disruptions and find information about stops and places on-the-go. There’s no mention of any of the Personal Intelligence features that were announced yesterday for Gemini in Android Auto and cars with Google built-in, however, which enable the voice assistant to access user information from Google apps, including Gmail, Calendar, Maps, Photos, YouTube, and Search. We’ve asked Google if CarPlay users will also receive the personalization update and will update if we hear back.

Cars with native Android Automotive OS will get Gemini later, with Polestar already signalling it will adopt the system in a future software update.

Gemini can also stay chatty if you’re after a bit of rolling companionship.
Google frames it as a tool that can “help you learn something new, brainstorm ideas, rehearse for important moments and much more.”
Gemini appears on the car’s infotainment screen once the companion app is installed on the driver’s Android phone.
From there, Google says the system can finally manage proper back-and-forth dialogue: navigation queries, messaging, calendar checks, to-do lists and even digging useful details out of your inbox.

Gemini appears on the car’s infotainment screen once the companion app is installed on the driver’s Android phone. Activation is familiar territory: say “Hey Google”, tap the on-screen mic or long-press the steering-wheel voice button. From there, Google says the system can finally manage proper back-and-forth dialogue: navigation queries, messaging, calendar checks, to-do lists and even digging useful details out of your inbox. Guemmy Kim, Senior Director of Product & User Experience for Android for Cars, told users to expect a “truly conversational” helper, adding that “you can just speak naturally, have a back and forth conversation and get more complex tasks done.” That includes asking it to find dinner spots by cuisine, send a friend your ETA with an emoji for flourish or hunt down that address hiding somewhere in last week’s emails. Gemini can also stay chatty if you’re after a bit of rolling companionship. Google frames it as a tool that can “help you learn something new, brainstorm ideas, rehearse for important moments and much more.” If you’re running Apple CarPlay, this update won’t reach you. Google spokesperson Sofia Giovannello confirmed there are “no updates to share” about Apple integration. Cars with native Android Automotive OS will get Gemini later, with Polestar already signalling it will adopt the system in a future software update. Voice control has long been sold as a safer bridge between tech and driving, though the science is still catching up. Early research points to only moderate cognitive load from in-car voice assistants, or better than staring at a handset, but not exactly risk-free. With far more capable AI now entering the cabin, expect fresh debate on whether all this extra chatter sharpens focus or gently siphons it away. For now, Android Auto drivers gain a sharper, chattier AI assistant riding shotgun, one that might make errands smoother, or at least make the morning commute feel slightly less lonely. relevantPassages.text: After introducing its Gemini AI assistant to Android Auto last year, Google is now bringing it to Apple CarPlay users.
The conversational Gemini in navigation is available today for US drivers, with “rollout happening globally too,” according to Google (we’ve asked for specific regional availability details).
Google describes this CarPlay support update as a conversational way to report traffic disruptions and find information about stops and places on-the-go.

sources.title: Google's Gemini AI assistant rolls into Android Auto - Driven Car Guide
passages: Google has begun pushing its Gemini AI assistant into cars running Android Auto, promising smarter conversations, quicker tasks and fewer moments of fumbling with your phone while trying to merge.
Gemini launches on Android Auto with navigation, messaging and task support.
Google spokesperson Sofia Giovannello confirmed there are “no updates to share” about Apple integration.
Cars with native Android Automotive OS will get Gemini later, with Polestar already signalling it will adopt the system in a future software update.
DRIVEN Car Guide is the first stop for any Kiwi looking to buy their next car.
Android Auto has a new co-pilot, and it talks a lot more like a human than the old one ever did.
Gemini can also stay chatty if you’re after a bit of rolling companionship.
Google frames it as a tool that can “help you learn something new, brainstorm ideas, rehearse for important moments and much more.”
Gemini appears on the car’s infotainment screen once the companion app is installed on the driver’s Android phone.
From there, Google says the system can finally manage proper back-and-forth dialogue: navigation queries, messaging, calendar checks, to-do lists and even digging useful details out of your inbox.

Android Auto has a new co-pilot, and it talks a lot more like a human than the old one ever did. Google has begun pushing its Gemini AI assistant into cars running Android Auto, promising smarter conversations, quicker tasks and fewer moments of fumbling with your phone while trying to merge. Gemini appears on the car’s infotainment screen once the companion app is installed on the driver’s Android phone. Activation is familiar territory: say “Hey Google”, tap the on-screen mic or long-press the steering-wheel voice button. From there, Google says the system can finally manage proper back-and-forth dialogue: navigation queries, messaging, calendar checks, to-do lists and even digging useful details out of your inbox. Guemmy Kim, Senior Director of Product & User Experience for Android for Cars, told users to expect a “truly conversational” helper, adding that “you can just speak naturally, have a back and forth conversation and get more complex tasks done.” That includes asking it to find dinner spots by cuisine, send a friend your ETA with an emoji for flourish or hunt down that address hiding somewhere in last week’s emails. Gemini can also stay chatty if you’re after a bit of rolling companionship. Google frames it as a tool that can “help you learn something new, brainstorm ideas, rehearse for important moments and much more.” If you’re running Apple CarPlay, this update won’t reach you. Google spokesperson Sofia Giovannello confirmed there are “no updates to share” about Apple integration. Cars with native Android Automotive OS will get Gemini later, with Polestar already signalling it will adopt the system in a future software update. Voice control has long been sold as a safer bridge between tech and driving, though the science is still catching up. Early research points to only moderate cognitive load from in-car voice assistants, or better than staring at a handset, but not exactly risk-free. With far more capable AI now entering the cabin, expect fresh debate on whether all this extra chatter sharpens focus or gently siphons it away. For now, Android Auto drivers gain a sharper, chattier AI assistant riding shotgun, one that might make errands smoother, or at least make the morning commute feel slightly less lonely. sources.title: Elon Musk says Tesla and SpaceX are weighing a $3.5 trillion merger—without him in the room - Yahoo Finance
passages: At Tuesday's closing prices, a combined Tesla-SpaceX would have a total market value of about $3.5 trillion, with SpaceX at about $2 trillion and Tesla at nearly $1.5 trillion.
A formal deal price wouldn't come until much further down the road, if at all.
Musk would own about a third of the combined entity.
The companies are already financially entangled, including a $2 billion investment by Tesla in SpaceX, Tesla's Monday proxy statement confirmed.
It's official: Tesla and SpaceX are in talks.
Independent board members at the two Elon Musk-led companies have formed special committees to hash over a possible merger, Musk told investors during SpaceX's third-quarter earnings call Tuesday.
Musk said the committees haven't reached any kind of an agreement on the terms of a potential transaction, and there's no guarantee that they will.
He noted that "some people out there assume that a SpaceX and Tesla merger is a certainty, and I think that would be overstating it." Musk also has to walk a fine line as a conflicted party.
As the CEO of both companies, he owns a roughly 20% stake in Tesla and 45% of SpaceX—and wields control over about 82% of the voting power at the latter.

Tesla stock rose just over 1% in after hours trading, while SpaceX rose above 5% following the Q&A with Wall Street analysts featuring Musk, SpaceX president and COO Gwynne Shotwell, and chief financial officer Bret Johnsen.

And Tesla board member James Murdoch, who has been a director at the electric-vehicle maker since 2017, testified in a previous legal challenge over Musk's pay package at Tesla that he had previously invested in SpaceX.
Tesla filed its annual shareholder proxy report on Monday, and it doesn't include a merger proposal for shareholders to vote on.
Rumors of a tie-up, however, have swirled for months, even before SpaceX's blockbuster IPO in June.

In his usual fashion, Musk offered up aggressively optimistic thoughts about the future of SpaceX, claiming SpaceX's breakneck buildout pace implies annual recurring revenue of $500 billion to $1 trillion by the end of 2027.
Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading.
At its third-quarter pace, SpaceX is bringing in about $58 billion a year.
Hitting the $100 billion figure would take about $8.3 billion of revenue in December, roughly 70% more than its average month last quarter.
Musk's range would require about $42 billion to $83 billion a month by December 2027.

Revenue from SpaceX's AI business, which was renamed "Super Intelligence," nearly tripled from the second quarter to $7.56 billion, surpassing Starlink's $5.25 billion for the first time since the company went public.
The disclosure from Musk came as SpaceX reported its first operating profit since its June IPO.
Tesla did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

It's official: Tesla and SpaceX are in talks. Independent board members at the two Elon Musk-led companies have formed special committees to hash over a possible merger, Musk told investors during SpaceX's third-quarter earnings call Tuesday.

"These special committees consist of independent directors, and because I'm a conflicted party, I can't actually be in the discussions of the special committees," said Musk, who was asked about a potential combination during the call. "This is definitely the kind of question where I feel like I'm tap dancing through a minefield."

Tesla stock rose just over 1% in after hours trading, while SpaceX rose above 5% following the Q&A with Wall Street analysts featuring Musk, SpaceX president and COO Gwynne Shotwell, and chief financial officer Bret Johnsen.

Musk said the committees haven't reached any kind of an agreement on the terms of a potential transaction, and there's no guarantee that they will. He noted that "some people out there assume that a SpaceX and Tesla merger is a certainty, and I think that would be overstating it." Musk also has to walk a fine line as a conflicted party. As the CEO of both companies, he owns a roughly 20% stake in Tesla and 45% of SpaceX—and wields control over about 82% of the voting power at the latter.
"It's an odd kabuki dance where two groups of people are talking and I can't be in the conversation," said Musk.

At the same time, Musk has made clear he believes a tie-up would be a fine idea. He cited collaboration on AI software, chip design, robotics, and connectivity, plus the planned Terafab chip plant, which is a colossal manufacturing complex being developed by SpaceX and Tesla jointly.

The committees were formed "at the request of shareholders," said Musk and on the Tesla side it would need support from a majority of all outstanding shares, which Musk described as "quite a high hurdle."

Tesla filed its annual shareholder proxy report on Monday, and it doesn't include a merger proposal for shareholders to vote on. Rumors of a tie-up, however, have swirled for months, even before SpaceX's blockbuster IPO in June.

At Tuesday's closing prices, a combined Tesla-SpaceX would have a total market value of about $3.5 trillion, with SpaceX at about $2 trillion and Tesla at nearly $1.5 trillion. A formal deal price wouldn't come until much further down the road, if at all. Musk would own about a third of the combined entity. The companies are already financially entangled, including a $2 billion investment by Tesla in SpaceX, Tesla's Monday proxy statement confirmed.
There are also multiple areas of overlap between the Tesla and SpaceX boards.

Ira Ehrenpreis, founder of venture capital firm DBL Partners, chairs SpaceX's compensation and nominating committee, which is a single committee at SpaceX, as well as the two separate committees at Tesla. And Tesla board member James Murdoch, who has been a director at the electric-vehicle maker since 2017, testified in a previous legal challenge over Musk's pay package at Tesla that he had previously invested in SpaceX.
The disclosure from Musk came as SpaceX reported its first operating profit since its June IPO.

Revenues for the third quarter fiscal 2027 year rose 161% to $14.58 billion, well above the $12.86 billion analysts expected, according to Visible Alpha consensus from S&P Global Market Intelligence. Operating revenue clocked in at $2.79 billion, apnd net income was $4.4 billion.

Revenue from SpaceX's AI business, which was renamed "Super Intelligence," nearly tripled from the second quarter to $7.56 billion, surpassing Starlink's $5.25 billion for the first time since the company went public.

In his usual fashion, Musk offered up aggressively optimistic thoughts about the future of SpaceX, claiming SpaceX's breakneck buildout pace implies annual recurring revenue of $500 billion to $1 trillion by the end of 2027. Meanwhile, Johnsen reaffirmed a target of $100 billion in annualized revenue by the end of this year.

At its third-quarter pace, SpaceX is bringing in about $58 billion a year. Hitting the $100 billion figure would take about $8.3 billion of revenue in December, roughly 70% more than its average month last quarter. Musk's range would require about $42 billion to $83 billion a month by December 2027.
Tesla did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

sources.title: SpaceX and Tesla boards form special committees to review merger
passages: The boards of SpaceX and Tesla have each formed special committees to review a possible merger.
The special committees, which consist of independent directors, were created at the request of shareholders, according to Elon Musk, CEO and the largest individual shareholder of both companies.

Tesla has seven independent board members under Nasdaq’s listing standards, including board chair Robyn Denholm; Ira Ehrenpreis, who is also a committee chair; former Tesla CTO JB Straubel; Joe Gebbia; Jack Hartung; James Murdoch; and Kathleen Wilson-Thompson, according to the company’s October 19 proxy filing .
It is a much bigger hurdle over at Tesla, where the company would need a 50% vote from all shareholders, not just those who vote, Musk noted.
Antonio Gracias, Musk, and SpaceX president and chief operating officer Gwynne Shotwell are also on the board, but not considered independent.
Gracias, who once sat on Tesla’s board, founded and leads Valor Equity Partners, which has a 3.4% stake in SpaceX.
Gracias’ firm also financed SpaceX’s AI hardware purchases through leaseback arrangements.

The special committees, which consist of independent directors, were created at the request of shareholders, according to Elon Musk, CEO and the largest individual shareholder of both companies. “Because I’m a conflicted party, I can’t actually be in the discussions of the special committees, so it’s this sort of a … It’s an odd kabuki dance where two groups of people are talking, and I can’t be in the conversation,” Musk said in response to a question during SpaceX’s third-quarter earnings call. Musk didn’t name the members of these special committees, only noting that they were independent directors. Tesla has seven independent board members under Nasdaq’s listing standards, including board chair Robyn Denholm; Ira Ehrenpreis, who is also a committee chair; former Tesla CTO JB Straubel; Joe Gebbia; Jack Hartung; James Murdoch; and Kathleen Wilson-Thompson, according to the company’s October 19 proxy filing . Neither Musk nor his brother Kimbal Musk is independent. Denholm, Gebbia, Ehrenpreis, Hartung, Murdoch, and Wilson-Thompson sit on a variety of established committees overseeing audit, compensation, and corporate governance. SpaceX lists six independent directors , including Ehrenpreis, who is also the chair of the company’s compensation and nominating committee. Randy Glein, Donald Harrison, Steve Jurvetson, Luke Nosek, and Roelof Botha are also considered independent directors. Antonio Gracias, Musk, and SpaceX president and chief operating officer Gwynne Shotwell are also on the board, but not considered independent. Gracias, who once sat on Tesla’s board, founded and leads Valor Equity Partners, which has a 3.4% stake in SpaceX. Gracias’ firm also financed SpaceX’s AI hardware purchases through leaseback arrangements. Musk said he supports the idea of the merger but cautioned that it is not a guaranteed outcome. “I think some people out there assume that a SpaceX and Tesla Motor is a certainty, and I think that would be overstating it,” he said, adding that he thinks it would be a good idea. “At the end of the day, the shareholders have to be supportive of this.” The special committees have not reached agreement on the terms of any transactions, he said. The SpaceX IPO cemented Musk’s grip on the company — he has more than 50% voting power — which would make it easier to garner support for a merger from SpaceX shareholders. It is a much bigger hurdle over at Tesla, where the company would need a 50% vote from all shareholders, not just those who vote, Musk noted. “I do think there’s a lot of merit to combining the companies as we are pretty much in the superintelligence singularity,” Musk said, adding there was a lot to be gaining from cooperating on developing AI software, robotics, SpaceX’s orbital AI data center project Starmind, and Terafab, the joint chip manufacturing project between Tesla and SpaceX. Musk didn’t name the members of these special committees, only noting that they were independent directors. Tesla has seven independent board members under Nasdaq’s listing standards, including board chair Robyn Denholm; Ira Ehrenpreis, who is also a committee chair; former Tesla CTO JB Straubel; Joe Gebbia; Jack Hartung; James Murdoch; and Kathleen Wilson-Thompson, according to the company’s October 19 proxy filing .

Neither Musk nor his brother Kimbal Musk is independent. Denholm, Gebbia, Ehrenpreis, Hartung, Murdoch, and Wilson-Thompson sit on a variety of established committees overseeing audit, compensation, and corporate governance.

SpaceX lists six independent directors , including Ehrenpreis, who is also the chair of the company’s compensation and nominating committee. Randy Glein, Donald Harrison, Steve Jurvetson, Luke Nosek, and Roelof Botha are also considered independent directors.

Antonio Gracias, Musk, and SpaceX president and chief operating officer Gwynne Shotwell are also on the board, but not considered independent. Gracias, who once sat on Tesla’s board, founded and leads Valor Equity Partners, which has a 3.4% stake in SpaceX. Gracias’ firm also financed SpaceX’s AI hardware purchases through leaseback arrangements.
Musk said he supports the idea of the merger but cautioned that it is not a guaranteed outcome.

“I think some people out there assume that a SpaceX and Tesla Motor is a certainty, and I think that would be overstating it,” he said, adding that he thinks it would be a good idea. “At the end of the day, the shareholders have to be supportive of this.”
The special committees have not reached agreement on the terms of any transactions, he said.

The SpaceX IPO cemented Musk’s grip on the company — he has more than 50% voting power — which would make it easier to garner support for a merger from SpaceX shareholders. It is a much bigger hurdle over at Tesla, where the company would need a 50% vote from all shareholders, not just those who vote, Musk noted.

“I do think there’s a lot of merit to combining the companies as we are pretty much in the superintelligence singularity,” Musk said, adding there was a lot to be gaining from cooperating on developing AI software, robotics, SpaceX’s orbital AI data center project Starmind, and Terafab, the joint chip manufacturing project between Tesla and SpaceX.

Elon Musk said SpaceX and Tesla formed special committees to study a potential merger as an initial step toward what he described as a deal that could become the largest of its kind in history. Musk told investors on a call that he sees “a lot to be gained through collaboration on developing superintelligent software,” and he said he is not participating in the committees’ discussions because of conflicts of interest. SpaceX reported a 161% revenue jump in the third quarter to $14.6 billion, and Musk said the company is expanding its computing capacity as it pursues AI-related growth.

SpaceX’s results call also placed Starlink’s satellite Internet unit as a continuing financial engine, with Starlink revenue rising 69% to $5.2 billion and its consumer subscriber base reaching 13.6 million. Musk added that the committees have not yet agreed on the terms of a merger transaction, and he said there is no guarantee of a deal.

Elon Musk said on Tuesday, “I think it would be a good idea,” while also stressing that “it’s really up to the special committees of both companies.” Musk told investors, “Because I’m a conflicted party, I can’t actually be in the discussion of the special committees,” and he said shareholders ultimately would need to approve any deal. Musk described the approval hurdle for Tesla as requiring the support of 50% of all Tesla shareholders, not just those voting, and he called that bar “quite a high hurdle.”

SpaceX’s third-quarter profit and spending figures framed the merger talk, with SpaceX posting net income of $4.4 billion and investing $19.6 billion during the quarter, including $16.4 billion in AI. Musk also tied the merger idea to AI and chip work, saying the companies could benefit from working together in areas such as artificial intelligence (AI), chip design, robotics and space-based computing.

SpaceX’s earnings call positioned AI as the driver of the quarter’s results, with AI revenue rising more than ninefold to $7.6 billion and overtaking Starlink as the largest source of revenue. Musk said the merger discussions are not certain, and he warned that “I think that would be overstating it,” while also describing the companies as being “pretty much in the superintelligence singularity.” The approval process remained central, with Musk saying at least 50% of Tesla’s shareholders would need to approve the merger, which he described as “quite a high hurdle to achieve.”

Analysts and market participants tracked the possibility of timing, with Barclays suggesting last week that an announcement could come before Tesla’s annual meeting in December. Musk’s comments left the committees as the immediate decision-makers, and the sources said the committees have been formed to examine the proposal at shareholders’ request while discussions had not produced any agreed terms.

As the CEO of both companies, he owns a roughly 20% stake in Tesla and 45% of SpaceX—and wields control over about 82% of the voting power at the latter.
"It's an odd kabuki dance where two groups of people are talking and I can't be in the conversation," said Musk.

At the same time, Musk has made clear he believes a tie-up would be a fine idea. He cited collaboration on AI software, chip design, robotics, and connectivity, plus the planned Terafab chip plant, which is a colossal manufacturing complex being developed by SpaceX and Tesla jointly.

The committees were formed "at the request of shareholders," said Musk and on the Tesla side it would need support from a majority of all outstanding shares, which Musk described as "quite a high hurdle."

Musk said the committees haven't reached any kind of an agreement on the terms of a potential transaction, and there's no guarantee that they will.
He noted that "some people out there assume that a SpaceX and Tesla merger is a certainty, and I think that would be overstating it." Musk also has to walk a fine line as a conflicted party.
As the CEO of both companies, he owns a roughly 20% stake in Tesla and 45% of SpaceX—and wields control over about 82% of the voting power at the latter.

Tesla stock rose just over 1% in after hours trading, while SpaceX rose above 5% following the Q&A with Wall Street analysts featuring Musk, SpaceX president and COO Gwynne Shotwell, and chief financial officer Bret Johnsen.

And Tesla board member James Murdoch, who has been a director at the electric-vehicle maker since 2017, testified in a previous legal challenge over Musk's pay package at Tesla that he had previously invested in SpaceX.
Tesla filed its annual shareholder proxy report on Monday, and it doesn't include a merger proposal for shareholders to vote on.
Rumors of a tie-up, however, have swirled for months, even before SpaceX's blockbuster IPO in June.

In his usual fashion, Musk offered up aggressively optimistic thoughts about the future of SpaceX, claiming SpaceX's breakneck buildout pace implies annual recurring revenue of $500 billion to $1 trillion by the end of 2027.

At its third-quarter pace, SpaceX is bringing in about $58 billion a year.
Hitting the $100 billion figure would take about $8.3 billion of revenue in December, roughly 70% more than its average month last quarter.
Musk's range would require about $42 billion to $83 billion a month by December 2027.

Revenue from SpaceX's AI business, which was renamed "Super Intelligence," nearly tripled from the second quarter to $7.56 billion, surpassing Starlink's $5.25 billion for the first time since the company went public.
The disclosure from Musk came as SpaceX reported its first operating profit since its June IPO.
Tesla did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

extraction.body: The boards of SpaceX and Tesla have each formed special committees to review a possible merger. The special committees, which consist of independent directors, were created at the request of shareholders, according to Elon Musk, CEO and the largest individual shareholder of both companies. “Because I’m a conflicted party, I can’t actually be in the discussions of the special committees, so it’s this sort of a … It’s an odd kabuki dance where two groups of people are talking, and I can’t be in the conversation,” Musk said in response to a question during SpaceX’s third-quarter earnings call. Musk didn’t name the members of these special committees, only noting that they were independent directors. Tesla has seven independent board members under Nasdaq’s listing standards, including board chair Robyn Denholm; Ira Ehrenpreis, who is also a committee chair; former Tesla CTO JB Straubel; Joe Gebbia; Jack Hartung; James Murdoch; and Kathleen Wilson-Thompson, according to the company’s October 19 proxy filing . Neither Musk nor his brother Kimbal Musk is independent. Denholm, Gebbia, Ehrenpreis, Hartung, Murdoch, and Wilson-Thompson sit on a variety of established committees overseeing audit, compensation, and corporate governance. SpaceX lists six independent directors , including Ehrenpreis, who is also the chair of the company’s compensation and nominating committee. Randy Glein, Donald Harrison, Steve Jurvetson, Luke Nosek, and Roelof Botha are also considered independent directors. Antonio Gracias, Musk, and SpaceX president and chief operating officer Gwynne Shotwell are also on the board, but not considered independent. Gracias, who once sat on Tesla’s board, founded and leads Valor Equity Partners, which has a 3.4% stake in SpaceX. Gracias’ firm also financed SpaceX’s AI hardware purchases through leaseback arrangements. Musk said he supports the idea of the merger but cautioned that it is not a guaranteed outcome. “I think some people out there assume that a SpaceX and Tesla Motor is a certainty, and I think that would be overstating it,” he said, adding that he thinks it would be a good idea. “At the end of the day, the shareholders have to be supportive of this.” The special committees have not reached agreement on the terms of any transactions, he said. The SpaceX IPO cemented Musk’s grip on the company — he has more than 50% voting power — which would make it easier to garner support for a merger from SpaceX shareholders. It is a much bigger hurdle over at Tesla, where the company would need a 50% vote from all shareholders, not just those who vote, Musk noted. “I do think there’s a lot of merit to combining the companies as we are pretty much in the superintelligence singularity,” Musk said, adding there was a lot to be gaining from cooperating on developing AI software, robotics, SpaceX’s orbital AI data center project Starmind, and Terafab, the joint chip manufacturing project between Tesla and SpaceX.
