Elon Musk said SpaceX and Tesla formed special committees to study a potential merger as an initial step toward what he described as a deal that could become the largest of its kind in history. Musk told investors on a call that he sees “a lot to be gained through collaboration on developing superintelligent software,” and he said he is not participating in the committees’ discussions because of conflicts of interest. SpaceX reported a 161% revenue jump in the third quarter to $14.6 billion, and Musk said the company is expanding its computing capacity as it pursues AI-related growth.

SpaceX’s results call also placed Starlink’s satellite Internet unit as a continuing financial engine, with Starlink revenue rising 69% to $5.2 billion and its consumer subscriber base reaching 13.6 million. Musk added that the committees have not yet agreed on the terms of a merger transaction, and he said there is no guarantee of a deal.

Elon Musk said on Tuesday, “I think it would be a good idea,” while also stressing that “it’s really up to the special committees of both companies.” Musk told investors, “Because I’m a conflicted party, I can’t actually be in the discussion of the special committees,” and he said shareholders ultimately would need to approve any deal. Musk described the approval hurdle for Tesla as requiring the support of 50% of all Tesla shareholders, not just those voting, and he called that bar “quite a high hurdle.”

SpaceX’s third-quarter profit and spending figures framed the merger talk, with SpaceX posting net income of $4.4 billion and investing $19.6 billion during the quarter, including $16.4 billion in AI. Musk also tied the merger idea to AI and chip work, saying the companies could benefit from working together in areas such as artificial intelligence (AI), chip design, robotics and space-based computing.

SpaceX’s earnings call positioned AI as the driver of the quarter’s results, with AI revenue rising more than ninefold to $7.6 billion and overtaking Starlink as the largest source of revenue. Musk said the merger discussions are not certain, and he warned that “I think that would be overstating it,” while also describing the companies as being “pretty much in the superintelligence singularity.” The approval process remained central, with Musk saying at least 50% of Tesla’s shareholders would need to approve the merger, which he described as “quite a high hurdle to achieve.”

Analysts and market participants tracked the possibility of timing, with Barclays suggesting last week that an announcement could come before Tesla’s annual meeting in December. Musk’s comments left the committees as the immediate decision-makers, and the sources said the committees have been formed to examine the proposal at shareholders’ request while discussions had not produced any agreed terms.

The new foldable iPhone Duo is on display during Apple's event at the Steve Jobs Theater in Cupertino, California, U.S. September 9, 2026. REUTERS/Carlos Barria

SAN FRANCISCO, Oct 21 (Reuters) - Apple on Wednesday said it will have 'limited' numbers of its folding iPhone Duo phone available for walk-in customers when the device launches Friday, after initial online orders sold out in minutes and pushed delivery times for some customers to January.

Apple announced its first folding phone in September, with analysts expecting it to quickly come to dominate a niche segment where rivals such as Samsung Electronics and Huawei Technologies have sold premium offerings for years.
But the iPhone Duo is also a more complex product than standard candy-bar iPhones, with a tight-fitting hinge that analysts believe may take time for Apple to learn to manufacture in high volumes.

“On Friday morning, our teams look forward to welcoming customers at Apple Stores to experience iPhone Duo and the incredible iPhone line-up for themselves," Apple said in a statement. "Apple Stores will have limited iPhone Duo available for walk-in customers, and we’re working hard to get this revolutionary new product into customers' hands as quickly as possible.”

The availability of walk-in units will vary by country, Apple said. Online order pickup and limited walk-in purchases will be available in the United States, Australia, Canada, Mexico and much of the UK and Europe.

But other regions will only have iPhone Duo units available for customers who already bought them online. Those include mainland China, France, Hong Kong, India, Japan, Malaysia, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand and the UAE, Apple said.
On the China-governed island of Macau, the iPhone Duo will be available for walk-in customers only, with limited inventory, Apple said.
(Reporting by Stephen Nellis in San Francisco, Editing by Franklin Paul)

extraction.body: Crucial vulnerabilities in a programming language that underpins much of the internet are so severe that European and British authorities have recommended websites temporarily go offline until they can be fixed. The flaws are in PHP, a little-known but crucial programming language which powers how web servers process code. The security team that maintains PHP released patches to fix the problem around 10 a.m. But several websites were temporarily down as of Wednesday morning, citing fear that hackers could take them over. Two massive but largely unmoderated forum sites, 4Chan and Something Awful, both went offline to wait for a patch. Japanese websites were also voluntarily offline, including systems for daycare centers and video games, the Japanese tech news site ITmedia reported. PHP is used in 69% of all websites, according to W3Techs, which surveys the software behind how the internet works. OpenAI said that it helped discover the vulnerability and brought it to PHP’s attention before hackers exploited it more severely. “Given the severity of these flaws and PHP’s widespread use, we consider this one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory,” the company wrote in a blog post Wednesday. “It highlights how AI can uncover security flaws with internet-scale impact, but the same capabilities can also help attackers rapidly develop offensive tools and exploits.” The vulnerability was discovered through OpenAI’s program to give cybersecurity companies access to ChatGPT models that are adept at finding software flaws, the company said. As websites around the world patched the flaws Wednesday, it was unclear how severely hackers were already exploiting it. Patchstack, a cybersecurity platform, said it had received “reports of active exploitation.” The chief technical officer of Cloudflare, one of the internet’s largest website hosting companies, wrote on X, “We are seeing early attacks emerging and are updating mitigations as new vectors show up.” Government agencies around the world, including the U.S. National Security Agency, have warned of the flaws and recommended potentially taking sites offline until they’re fixed. CERT-EU, the European Union’s technical cybersecurity advisory body, said, “Organisations should consider isolating internet-facing applications from public networks until a fix is available.” The United Kingdom’s National Cyber Security Centre recommended, “Where immediate remediation is not feasible, organisations should consider taking the system offline until it can be fully mitigated.” The primary U.S. cybersecurity agency, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, said in an advisory late Wednesday morning that it recommended patching the software flaws, but that it had “not observed exploitation of these vulnerabilities as of the time of publication.”

Patchstack, a cybersecurity platform, said it had received “reports of active exploitation.” The chief technical officer of Cloudflare, one of the internet’s largest website hosting companies, wrote on X, “We are seeing early attacks emerging and are updating mitigations as new vectors show up.” Government agencies around the world, including the U.S.
National Security Agency, have warned of the flaws and recommended potentially taking sites offline until they’re fixed.

extraction.body: The developers of the PHP programming language, which is extensively used across the internet, said on Wednesday a set of new ​updates fixing two previously identified critical vulnerabilities was now ​live. It strongly encouraged ‌users to update software immediately. Those unable to apply key fixes to the widely used software should also consider taking their websites down, UK and international cybersecurity officials have warned. Concerns have escalated in recent days that websites running software would be exposed to serious cyber intrusions. PHP said both vulnerabilities were rated 9.2 on the CVSS v4.0 severity scale and urged users to "upgrade as soon as the release is available". Government websites in Europe and ‌elsewhere went offline on Wednesday as organisations scrambled to protect their systems. Users visiting these websites were told there was "ongoing maintenance". Also, government agencies in the Netherlands and Finland were among those which took sites offline as a precaution. The ‌Wikimedia Foundation, which ‌runs online encyclopedia Wikipedia, was one company on Wednesday which said it was ‌in the process of addressing ​security vulnerabilities in the PHP programming ​language. The European Union ‌Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-EU) said on Tuesday that the 9.2 rating indicated a risk of unauthenticated remote code execution, a type of flaw that can allow attackers to run malicious code on vulnerable systems without logging in. It urged organisations to prepare for the immediate patching of affected assets and said those unable to do so should consider taking their sites offline. Sky News' science and technology editor, Tom Clarke , said: "The first thing to get across is the scale; from Belgium, Germany, France, the Netherlands, and Australia's government websites are being taken offline. "It's important to say this is not because of a hack, it's because of a vulnerability that has been discovered by cyber security companies and communicated globally by national cyber security agencies - but is a vulnerability so widespread across the internet that it affects government websites, as well as many businesses as well. "We are going to be seeing in the coming hours and days a huge effort to patch that vulnerability, before, now it's been made public, nefarious actors, hackers, might try to exploit it." Clarke said PHP is "quite an old programming language" but it is ingrained throughout the internet - with up to "70% of the world's web pages" having this language built into them. He noted UK government websites are not directly affected, but "ends of their system will be", for example council websites or small businesses, who may need to update their systems. Web hosting provider GoDaddy said the flaws could allow attackers to access affected servers which could potentially lead to data theft, website defacement or full system compromise. The Australian Cyber Security Centre (ACSC) urged organisations to ​identify PHP systems in their environments, prepare to apply patches and monitor applications for ​signs of malicious activity. Cybersecurity agencies in Britain and Japan are also among those urging PHP users to update immediately or take websites offline until patches can be applied. Dane Knecht, the chief technology officer of Web and cloud security firm Cloudflare, said that attacks were already happening and Cloudflare was updating its firewall ‌rules as a stopgap measure. He said on X: "We are seeing early attacks emerging and are updating mitigations as new vectors show up. Patch as soon as PHP releases the update." Don Smith, VP Threat Intelligence, Sophos Counter Threat Unit, said: "Security teams should prioritise internet-facing systems, confirming which versions are affected as soon as the official advisory is published, and apply the updates without delay. "Threat actors move fast, especially with the help of AI and this will likely be a priority target for them over the coming hours and days so it is crucial organisations monitor PHP and web-server processes for unusual processes, command execution or other signs that an attacker may already have gained a foothold."

PHP rates both CVSS v4.0 9.2 (Critical) . The fixed versions are PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 , released on 21 October 2026. PHP's GitHub security advisories were published at 13:34 UTC (16:34 Cyprus time), ahead of the scheduled 14:00 UTC release time. PHP's security advisory says "all PHP installations serving web requests" are at risk, including PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed. PHP considers the risk "highest for mod_php, with a demonstrated exploit where an unauthenticated request can trigger the attack before any application code runs." PHP says "There are no complete mitigations, updating is the only safe choice." PHP powers many websites and web applications, including content management systems, e-commerce platforms and custom web services (BleepingComputer), so it is very likely to be somewhere in your vendors' stacks. PHP describes the two flaws as follows (php.net security advisory and GitHub advisories): Both have the CVSS v4.0 vector AV:N/AC:H/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N (score 9.2) from PHP as CNA. For CVE-2026-109618, PHP says complete remote code execution "was validated over HTTP against mod_php", and that source analysis supports PHP-FPM as susceptible, "though no complete FPM exploit has been demonstrated". For CVE-2026-109619, PHP says "Session lifecycle RCE was validated against mod_php and FPM"; it adds that the FPM path "depends on a suitable application operation" ( GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp ). This advisory does not cover how to exploit the flaws. PHP's CVE records credit Ryan at Calif.io, Wiz and OpenAI with reporting or finding the flaws, and PHP developers Arnaud Le Blanc, Ilija Tovilo, Jakub Zelenka and Nora Dossche with the fix. NVD has not published its own score. Neither CVE is in CISA's KEV catalog (catalog version 2026.10.20, released 20 Oct 2026). None published. PHP, CERT-EU and the NCSC have released no indicators of compromise. Cloudflare says it was seeing early attacks before the release but has not published details. Rescana has not confirmed in-the-wild exploitation, and neither CVE is in CISA's KEV catalog as of this update. According to the Hacker News , the two critical PHP vulnerabilities would be disclosed on October 22.
The post described them as remote code execution flaws with CVSS scores of 10.0 and said they affected versions dating back to PHP 5.
Security Affairs newsletter Round 600 by Pierluigi Paganini – INTERNATIONAL EDITION

“Until PHP publishes an official advisory, security teams cannot determine which specific deployments face the greatest exposure; every organization running PHP in production should prepare to act quickly once a fix is confirmed.”
Internet-facing systems should take priority, particularly servers running business-critical applications or processing sensitive information.
Administrators should also check with their Linux distribution and hosting provider, since vendors sometimes backport security fixes without changing the upstream version number in the way expected.
Until the fixes become available, organizations should identify their PHP installations and prepare to install the correct update as soon as the vendor publishes it.
The PHP security team confirmed both vulnerabilities carry a CVSS v4.0 score of 9.2.

It hasn’t yet published their technical details, confirmed the affected versions, or identified the releases that will fix them. The official PHP announcement says the full information will accompany the security updates. “The PHP security team would like to give advance notice of an upcoming security release . It is scheduled for Wednesday, 21 October 2026 at 14:00 UTC. It addresses two critical vulnerabilities, both rated CVSS v4.0 9.2.” states the announcement . “All PHP users are encouraged to prepare now so they can upgrade as soon as the release is available. We reserve the right to release earlier should details of either vulnerability become public, or should evidence of active exploitation appear in the wild. Full details, affected versions, and the fixed versions will be published with the release.” Researchers dubbed the vulnerabilities as php2shell , using the identifiers CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. The identifiers and the claim that the flaws allow remote code execution come from reports outside PHP’s initial advisory, rather than from a published technical analysis by the project. According to the Hacker News , the two critical PHP vulnerabilities would be disclosed on October 22. The post described them as remote code execution flaws with CVSS scores of 10.0 and said they affected versions dating back to PHP 5. Researchers at watchTowr subsequently confirmed that the vulnerabilities were real and said the information had leaked before the agreed disclosure date. The company also reported that it had reproduced one of the flaws, CVE-2026-109618, but withheld technical details while patches remained unavailable. PHP published its advance security notice later that day, setting the release for Wednesday, October 21, one day before the date reported in the leak. The team also reserved the right to release the fixes earlier if technical details became public or it found evidence of active exploitation. The difference between the reported severity scores matters. The leaked information cited CVSS 10.0, while PHP officially rated both vulnerabilities 9.2 under CVSS version 4.0. Until the vendor publishes its technical advisory, the official score is the one administrators should use when describing PHP’s assessment. The main concern is the possibility that the flaws affect a wide range of PHP installations. Reports have suggested that versions from PHP 5 onward could be vulnerable, but watchTowr’s FAQ explicitly notes that the scope hasn’t been confirmed by an official vendor advisory. “The report claims the vulnerability affects every PHP version from PHP 5 onward, though this scope has not been confirmed by an official vendor advisory. extraction.body: Crucial vulnerabilities in a programming language that underpins much of the internet are so severe that European and British authorities have recommended websites temporarily go offline until they can be fixed. The flaws are in PHP, a little-known but crucial programming language which powers how web servers process code. The security team that maintains PHP released patches to fix the problem around 10 a.m. But several websites were temporarily down as of Wednesday morning, citing fear that hackers could take them over. Two massive but largely unmoderated forum sites, 4Chan and Something Awful, both went offline to wait for a patch. Japanese websites were also voluntarily offline, including systems for daycare centers and video games, the Japanese tech news site ITmedia reported. PHP is used in 69% of all websites, according to W3Techs, which surveys the software behind how the internet works. OpenAI said that it helped discover the vulnerability and brought it to PHP’s attention before hackers exploited it more severely. “Given the severity of these flaws and PHP’s widespread use, we consider this one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory,” the company wrote in a blog post Wednesday. “It highlights how AI can uncover security flaws with internet-scale impact, but the same capabilities can also help attackers rapidly develop offensive tools and exploits.” The vulnerability was discovered through OpenAI’s program to give cybersecurity companies access to ChatGPT models that are adept at finding software flaws, the company said. As websites around the world patched the flaws Wednesday, it was unclear how severely hackers were already exploiting it. Patchstack, a cybersecurity platform, said it had received “reports of active exploitation.” The chief technical officer of Cloudflare, one of the internet’s largest website hosting companies, wrote on X, “We are seeing early attacks emerging and are updating mitigations as new vectors show up.” Government agencies around the world, including the U.S. National Security Agency, have warned of the flaws and recommended potentially taking sites offline until they’re fixed. CERT-EU, the European Union’s technical cybersecurity advisory body, said, “Organisations should consider isolating internet-facing applications from public networks until a fix is available.” The United Kingdom’s National Cyber Security Centre recommended, “Where immediate remediation is not feasible, organisations should consider taking the system offline until it can be fully mitigated.” The primary U.S. cybersecurity agency, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, said in an advisory late Wednesday morning that it recommended patching the software flaws, but that it had “not observed exploitation of these vulnerabilities as of the time of publication.”

OpenAI said that it helped discover the vulnerability and brought it to PHP’s attention before hackers exploited it more severely.
“Given the severity of these flaws and PHP’s widespread use, we consider this one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory,” the company wrote in a blog post Wednesday.

“It highlights how AI can uncover security flaws with internet-scale impact, but the same capabilities can also help attackers rapidly develop offensive tools and exploits.” The vulnerability was discovered through OpenAI’s program to give cybersecurity companies access to ChatGPT models that are adept at finding software flaws, the company said.
As websites around the world patched the flaws Wednesday, it was unclear how severely hackers were already exploiting it.

Patchstack, a cybersecurity platform, said it had received “reports of active exploitation.” The chief technical officer of Cloudflare, one of the internet’s largest website hosting companies, wrote on X, “We are seeing early attacks emerging and are updating mitigations as new vectors show up.” Government agencies around the world, including the U.S.
National Security Agency, have warned of the flaws and recommended potentially taking sites offline until they’re fixed.

CERT-EU, the European Union’s technical cybersecurity advisory body, said, “Organisations should consider isolating internet-facing applications from public networks until a fix is available.” The United Kingdom’s National Cyber Security Centre recommended, “Where immediate remediation is not feasible, organisations should consider taking the system offline until it can be fully mitigated.” The primary U.S. cybersecurity agency, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, said in an advisory late Wednesday morning that it recommended patching the software flaws, but that it had “not observed exploitation of these vulnerabilities as of the time of publication.”

extraction.body: The developers of the PHP programming language, which is extensively used across the internet, said on Wednesday a set of new ​updates fixing two previously identified critical vulnerabilities was now ​live. It strongly encouraged ‌users to update software immediately. Those unable to apply key fixes to the widely used software should also consider taking their websites down, UK and international cybersecurity officials have warned. Concerns have escalated in recent days that websites running software would be exposed to serious cyber intrusions. PHP said both vulnerabilities were rated 9.2 on the CVSS v4.0 severity scale and urged users to "upgrade as soon as the release is available". Government websites in Europe and ‌elsewhere went offline on Wednesday as organisations scrambled to protect their systems. Users visiting these websites were told there was "ongoing maintenance". Also, government agencies in the Netherlands and Finland were among those which took sites offline as a precaution. The ‌Wikimedia Foundation, which ‌runs online encyclopedia Wikipedia, was one company on Wednesday which said it was ‌in the process of addressing ​security vulnerabilities in the PHP programming ​language. The European Union ‌Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-EU) said on Tuesday that the 9.2 rating indicated a risk of unauthenticated remote code execution, a type of flaw that can allow attackers to run malicious code on vulnerable systems without logging in. It urged organisations to prepare for the immediate patching of affected assets and said those unable to do so should consider taking their sites offline. Sky News' science and technology editor, Tom Clarke , said: "The first thing to get across is the scale; from Belgium, Germany, France, the Netherlands, and Australia's government websites are being taken offline. "It's important to say this is not because of a hack, it's because of a vulnerability that has been discovered by cyber security companies and communicated globally by national cyber security agencies - but is a vulnerability so widespread across the internet that it affects government websites, as well as many businesses as well. "We are going to be seeing in the coming hours and days a huge effort to patch that vulnerability, before, now it's been made public, nefarious actors, hackers, might try to exploit it." Clarke said PHP is "quite an old programming language" but it is ingrained throughout the internet - with up to "70% of the world's web pages" having this language built into them. He noted UK government websites are not directly affected, but "ends of their system will be", for example council websites or small businesses, who may need to update their systems. Web hosting provider GoDaddy said the flaws could allow attackers to access affected servers which could potentially lead to data theft, website defacement or full system compromise. The Australian Cyber Security Centre (ACSC) urged organisations to ​identify PHP systems in their environments, prepare to apply patches and monitor applications for ​signs of malicious activity. Cybersecurity agencies in Britain and Japan are also among those urging PHP users to update immediately or take websites offline until patches can be applied. Dane Knecht, the chief technology officer of Web and cloud security firm Cloudflare, said that attacks were already happening and Cloudflare was updating its firewall ‌rules as a stopgap measure. He said on X: "We are seeing early attacks emerging and are updating mitigations as new vectors show up. Patch as soon as PHP releases the update." Don Smith, VP Threat Intelligence, Sophos Counter Threat Unit, said: "Security teams should prioritise internet-facing systems, confirming which versions are affected as soon as the official advisory is published, and apply the updates without delay. "Threat actors move fast, especially with the help of AI and this will likely be a priority target for them over the coming hours and days so it is crucial organisations monitor PHP and web-server processes for unusual processes, command execution or other signs that an attacker may already have gained a foothold."

Both CVEs are published on cve.org; NVD received both records on 21 October and lists them as "Received", with no NVD score yet (it shows PHP's 9.2). PHP rates both CVSS v4.0 9.2 (Critical) . The fixed versions are PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 , released on 21 October 2026. PHP's GitHub security advisories were published at 13:34 UTC (16:34 Cyprus time), ahead of the scheduled 14:00 UTC release time. PHP's security advisory says "all PHP installations serving web requests" are at risk, including PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed. PHP considers the risk "highest for mod_php, with a demonstrated exploit where an unauthenticated request can trigger the attack before any application code runs." PHP says "There are no complete mitigations, updating is the only safe choice." PHP powers many websites and web applications, including content management systems, e-commerce platforms and custom web services (BleepingComputer), so it is very likely to be somewhere in your vendors' stacks. PHP describes the two flaws as follows (php.net security advisory and GitHub advisories): Both have the CVSS v4.0 vector AV:N/AC:H/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N (score 9.2) from PHP as CNA. For CVE-2026-109618, PHP says complete remote code execution "was validated over HTTP against mod_php", and that source analysis supports PHP-FPM as susceptible, "though no complete FPM exploit has been demonstrated". For CVE-2026-109619, PHP says "Session lifecycle RCE was validated against mod_php and FPM"; it adds that the FPM path "depends on a suitable application operation" ( GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp ). This advisory does not cover how to exploit the flaws. PHP's CVE records credit Ryan at Calif.io, Wiz and OpenAI with reporting or finding the flaws, and PHP developers Arnaud Le Blanc, Ilija Tovilo, Jakub Zelenka and Nora Dossche with the fix. NVD has not published its own score. Neither CVE is in CISA's KEV catalog (catalog version 2026.10.20, released 20 Oct 2026). None published. PHP, CERT-EU and the NCSC have released no indicators of compromise. Cloudflare says it was seeing early attacks before the release but has not published details. Rescana has not confirmed in-the-wild exploitation, and neither CVE is in CISA's KEV catalog as of this update. passages: PHP is preparing an emergency security release for two critical vulnerabilities that could let attackers execute code remotely on affected servers.
According to the Hacker News , the two critical PHP vulnerabilities would be disclosed on October 22.
The post described them as remote code execution flaws with CVSS scores of 10.0 and said they affected versions dating back to PHP 5.
Security Affairs newsletter Round 600 by Pierluigi Paganini – INTERNATIONAL EDITION

“Until PHP publishes an official advisory, security teams cannot determine which specific deployments face the greatest exposure; every organization running PHP in production should prepare to act quickly once a fix is confirmed.”
Internet-facing systems should take priority, particularly servers running business-critical applications or processing sensitive information.
Administrators should also check with their Linux distribution and hosting provider, since vendors sometimes backport security fixes without changing the upstream version number in the way expected.
Until the fixes become available, organizations should identify their PHP installations and prepare to install the correct update as soon as the vendor publishes it.
The PHP security team confirmed both vulnerabilities carry a CVSS v4.0 score of 9.2.

It hasn’t yet published their technical details, confirmed the affected versions, or identified the releases that will fix them. The official PHP announcement says the full information will accompany the security updates. “The PHP security team would like to give advance notice of an upcoming security release . It is scheduled for Wednesday, 21 October 2026 at 14:00 UTC. It addresses two critical vulnerabilities, both rated CVSS v4.0 9.2.” states the announcement . “All PHP users are encouraged to prepare now so they can upgrade as soon as the release is available. We reserve the right to release earlier should details of either vulnerability become public, or should evidence of active exploitation appear in the wild. Full details, affected versions, and the fixed versions will be published with the release.” Researchers dubbed the vulnerabilities as php2shell , using the identifiers CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. The identifiers and the claim that the flaws allow remote code execution come from reports outside PHP’s initial advisory, rather than from a published technical analysis by the project. According to the Hacker News , the two critical PHP vulnerabilities would be disclosed on October 22. The post described them as remote code execution flaws with CVSS scores of 10.0 and said they affected versions dating back to PHP 5. Researchers at watchTowr subsequently confirmed that the vulnerabilities were real and said the information had leaked before the agreed disclosure date. The company also reported that it had reproduced one of the flaws, CVE-2026-109618, but withheld technical details while patches remained unavailable. PHP published its advance security notice later that day, setting the release for Wednesday, October 21, one day before the date reported in the leak. Multiple cyber-security agencies have urged organisations unable to apply fixes in time to consider taking their sites down, leaving bodies such as the Finnish government, Edinburgh council and the BBC to take pages offline.
Finland has temporarily shut down the government's public web services, while the Netherlands' cyber-security agency said it was taking its own website offline due to the vulnerabilities.
Japan's national cyber-security office and EU cyber-security officials have issued a similar warning , external .
The flaws were discovered by AI, with cyber-security firm Wiz saying they were the "most severe vulnerabilities ever discovered" by the tech, which is reshaping the cyber landscape.
"We have taken down a number of other systems as a precautionary measure until they can be safely patched," it said.
The Netherlands' National Institute for Public Health and the Environment, an agency of the Dutch government, has taken down its website.

It ​quietly powers WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, and Magento sites, shared hosting platforms, control panels, and an awful ⁠lot of software that doesn't even advertise that it runs PHP under the hood," cyber-security company Huntress said.
Other websites, including the art platform DeviantArt, have said they are " temporarily down for maintenance , external " without specifying the reason.
"Frontier models were critical to making this process practical, enabling us to develop and adapt working exploits across multiple applications in hours," Wiz said in a blog post.
Such a cyber-attack could potentially allow hackers to install malware and take down websites.

extraction.body: International governments and agencies have urged websites to address two critical cyber-security flaws in a programming language which powers much of the internet. The vulnerabilities were found within the PHP programming language, with a fix issued on Wednesday afternoon. Multiple cyber-security agencies have urged organisations unable to apply fixes in time to consider taking their sites down, leaving bodies such as the Finnish government, Edinburgh council and the BBC to take pages offline. The flaws were discovered by AI, with cyber-security firm Wiz saying they were the "most severe vulnerabilities ever discovered" by the tech, which is reshaping the cyber landscape. Finland has temporarily shut down the government's public web services, while the Netherlands' cyber-security agency said it was taking its own website offline due to the vulnerabilities. The US National Security Agency issued similar advice on X , external for organisations to take their systems offline if they were unable to update with the fix. "These vulnerabilities often provide a direct path to the server's file system or database," it wrote. And in a post on X , external , Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi urged people to check if their publicly available websites ran on PHP. The Wikimedia Foundation, which runs the online encyclopedia Wikipedia, said it was addressing the security vulnerabilities. "We have taken down a number of other systems as a precautionary measure until they can be safely patched," it said. That led some people to be unable to access parts of Wikipedia on Wednesday. They have not confirmed a link to PHP - BBC News has approached them for comment. Other websites, including the art platform DeviantArt, have said they are " temporarily down for maintenance , external " without specifying the reason. The vulnerabilities were discovered by cyber-security researchers at the firms Calif and Wiz. They used state-of-the art AI, made by OpenAI, to find the flaws. OpenAI said in a blog post , external it was "one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory". According to the firms, they had gone undetected for more than a decade. "Frontier models were critical to making this process practical, enabling us to develop and adapt working exploits across multiple applications in hours," Wiz said in a blog post. It has estimated "roughly 70%" of the internet is affected, though the BBC is unable to verify that figure. The Netherlands' National Institute for Public Health and the Environment, an agency of the Dutch government, has taken down its website. Similarly the website of the Tweede Kamer, the lower house of the nation's parliament, has become inaccessible. The UK's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), as well as its counterparts in the EU and Australia have urged those who use PHP to apply the fixes. "Where immediate remediation is not feasible, organisations should consider taking the system offline until it can be fully mitigated," the NCSC said in a note , external . Japan's national cyber-security office and EU cyber-security officials have issued a similar warning , external . "PHP is everywhere. It ​quietly powers WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, and Magento sites, shared hosting platforms, control panels, and an awful ⁠lot of software that doesn't even advertise that it runs PHP under the hood," cyber-security company Huntress said. Cyber-security expert Don Smith, from the Sophos Counter Threat Unit, told the BBC this would "likely be a priority target" for hackers. The immediate challenge was not simply installing a patch to fix the issue, but finding and managing every instance where PHP was running, he said. "The use of PHP is pervasive, it can sit beneath public websites, content management systems, hosting platforms and third-party products, sometimes without even being obvious to the organisation using it," he said. He said it was crucial that organisations looked out for signs that an attacker "might have already have gained a foothold". The European Union Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-EU) said the risk scores given to the vulnerabilities "indicate the potential for unauthenticated remote code execution". Such a cyber-attack could potentially allow hackers to install malware and take down websites. Dane Knecht, chief technology officer at internet infrastructure firm Cloudflare, said he was , external "seeing early attacks emerging and are updating mitigations as new vectors show up". The NCSC said once organisations have installed the update, they should "continuously monitor for security updates from third-party software vendors, including for appliances and services that may bundle PHP". It is not yet clear which versions of the programming language are affected, but CERT-EU said it could affect all versions of it dating back to PHP 5 onwards - which launched in 2004. coreStoryFacts.text: Websites taken down worldwide as critical cyber-security update issued

Multiple cyber-security agencies have urged organisations unable to apply fixes in time to consider taking their sites down, leaving bodies such as the Finnish government, Edinburgh council and the BBC to take pages offline.
Finland has temporarily shut down the government's public web services, while the Netherlands' cyber-security agency said it was taking its own website offline due to the vulnerabilities.
Japan's national cyber-security office and EU cyber-security officials have issued a similar warning , external .
The flaws were discovered by AI, with cyber-security firm Wiz saying they were the "most severe vulnerabilities ever discovered" by the tech, which is reshaping the cyber landscape.
"We have taken down a number of other systems as a precautionary measure until they can be safely patched," it said.

It ​quietly powers WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, and Magento sites, shared hosting platforms, control panels, and an awful ⁠lot of software that doesn't even advertise that it runs PHP under the hood," cyber-security company Huntress said.

"Frontier models were critical to making this process practical, enabling us to develop and adapt working exploits across multiple applications in hours," Wiz said in a blog post.
Such a cyber-attack could potentially allow hackers to install malware and take down websites.

extraction.body: International governments and agencies have urged websites to address two critical cyber-security flaws in a programming language which powers much of the internet. The vulnerabilities were found within the PHP programming language, with a fix issued on Wednesday afternoon. Multiple cyber-security agencies have urged organisations unable to apply fixes in time to consider taking their sites down, leaving bodies such as the Finnish government, Edinburgh council and the BBC to take pages offline. The flaws were discovered by AI, with cyber-security firm Wiz saying they were the "most severe vulnerabilities ever discovered" by the tech, which is reshaping the cyber landscape. Finland has temporarily shut down the government's public web services, while the Netherlands' cyber-security agency said it was taking its own website offline due to the vulnerabilities. The US National Security Agency issued similar advice on X , external for organisations to take their systems offline if they were unable to update with the fix. "These vulnerabilities often provide a direct path to the server's file system or database," it wrote. And in a post on X , external , Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi urged people to check if their publicly available websites ran on PHP. The Wikimedia Foundation, which runs the online encyclopedia Wikipedia, said it was addressing the security vulnerabilities. "We have taken down a number of other systems as a precautionary measure until they can be safely patched," it said. That led some people to be unable to access parts of Wikipedia on Wednesday. They have not confirmed a link to PHP - BBC News has approached them for comment. Other websites, including the art platform DeviantArt, have said they are " temporarily down for maintenance , external " without specifying the reason. The vulnerabilities were discovered by cyber-security researchers at the firms Calif and Wiz. They used state-of-the art AI, made by OpenAI, to find the flaws. OpenAI said in a blog post , external it was "one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory". According to the firms, they had gone undetected for more than a decade. "Frontier models were critical to making this process practical, enabling us to develop and adapt working exploits across multiple applications in hours," Wiz said in a blog post. It has estimated "roughly 70%" of the internet is affected, though the BBC is unable to verify that figure. The Netherlands' National Institute for Public Health and the Environment, an agency of the Dutch government, has taken down its website. Similarly the website of the Tweede Kamer, the lower house of the nation's parliament, has become inaccessible. The UK's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), as well as its counterparts in the EU and Australia have urged those who use PHP to apply the fixes. "Where immediate remediation is not feasible, organisations should consider taking the system offline until it can be fully mitigated," the NCSC said in a note , external . Japan's national cyber-security office and EU cyber-security officials have issued a similar warning , external . "PHP is everywhere. It ​quietly powers WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, and Magento sites, shared hosting platforms, control panels, and an awful ⁠lot of software that doesn't even advertise that it runs PHP under the hood," cyber-security company Huntress said. Cyber-security expert Don Smith, from the Sophos Counter Threat Unit, told the BBC this would "likely be a priority target" for hackers. The immediate challenge was not simply installing a patch to fix the issue, but finding and managing every instance where PHP was running, he said. "The use of PHP is pervasive, it can sit beneath public websites, content management systems, hosting platforms and third-party products, sometimes without even being obvious to the organisation using it," he said. He said it was crucial that organisations looked out for signs that an attacker "might have already have gained a foothold". The European Union Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-EU) said the risk scores given to the vulnerabilities "indicate the potential for unauthenticated remote code execution". Such a cyber-attack could potentially allow hackers to install malware and take down websites. Dane Knecht, chief technology officer at internet infrastructure firm Cloudflare, said he was , external "seeing early attacks emerging and are updating mitigations as new vectors show up". The NCSC said once organisations have installed the update, they should "continuously monitor for security updates from third-party software vendors, including for appliances and services that may bundle PHP". It is not yet clear which versions of the programming language are affected, but CERT-EU said it could affect all versions of it dating back to PHP 5 onwards - which launched in 2004. extraction.body: The PHP development team has released emergency security updates to fix PHP2Shell, two critical vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) that could let attackers execute code remotely on web servers without logging in. The fixes are in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35, and the team is strongly urging all PHP users to update immediately. “These findings rank among the most severe vulnerabilities discovered in PHP, and arguably in software history. The underlying flaws had been present for decades, but demonstrating their exploitability required an exceptionally complex chain of steps, at the edge of what human researchers could practically achieve. Frontier AI models substantially reduced that barrier, turning a longstanding flaw into an exploit,” Wiz researchers explained . Every PHP installation that serves web requests is affected, including PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed. Setups using mod_php face the greatest danger. A working exploit has already shown that a single unauthenticated request can trigger the attack before any application code runs. “The PHP situation will lead to a mass of incidents – it’s one of the biggest vulns in years,” noted security researcher Kevin Beaumont. CVE-2026-109618 – RCE via OOM corruption : out-of-memory handling can interrupt PHP while internal request data is only partially initialized. Request cleanup may then treat the invalid data as valid. CVE-2026-109619 – RCE via stale global state : request-owned internal state can survive after its backing memory has been freed. A later request handled by the same worker may use that stale state before normal initialization resets it. The UK’s National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) is urging organizations to consider taking offline any system that can’t be fixed right away. “So many embedded installations out there that will never be patched. Too many forgotten, unmaintained apps. There will be a long tail for this one,” commented computer forensics expert Hal Pomeranz. Update to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35. Downloads are available here . Linux distributions and long-term support (LTS) vendors got the patches ahead of the public release, so admins should check with their vendor for updated packages. Anyone who relies on rpms.remirepo.net , a volunteer-maintained repository, is advised to switch to distribution packages or build PHP from source so they can patch immediately. The repository will not have updates available today. Because the vulnerabilities are so severe, the PHP security team has also released minimal source backports for PHP 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1. These are meant for people who build from source or who don’t have an LTS vendor. “PHP sites behind Cloudflare already have an initial set of WAF rules deployed for the known exploit vectors in these vulnerabilities. The rules are available to all customers, including free,” said Dane Knecht, CTO at Cloudflare.

passages: With 70% of the Internet affected, the impact of PHP2Shell cannot be overstated.
The vulnerable code had been there for more than a decade – what AI changed was the ability to understand the weaknesses and turn them into a working exploit.
With frontier AI models and the right tools, a single researcher completed in a week what previously would have taken a world-class team months of work.
Some vulnerabilities become turning points because they challenge fundamental assumptions about security.
In 2014, Heartbleed exposed the fragility of shared infrastructure securing the internet.
In 2021, Log4Shell revealed how deeply embedded software dependencies could create widespread exposure that organizations struggled to identify.
We believe PHP2Shell could mark a similar turning point for the AI era, illustrating how AI can change the practical exploitability of longstanding vulnerabilities.
Building the exploit required chaining multiple flaws and adapting to each target’s memory layout through repeated testing and debugging.
Frontier models were critical to making this process practical, enabling us to develop and adapt working exploits across multiple applications in hours.
As the time and expertise required for this work decrease, complexity may no longer provide a meaningful barrier, changing how we define what is vulnerable in practice.
Wiz Research uncovered multiple critical vulnerabilities in core PHP, a popular general-purpose scripting language that powers 70% of all websites in the world.
Successful exploitation could allow attackers to take control of affected servers, steal sensitive data, and deface the websites running on them.
Sensor customers using the newest version (1.0.12768) can also enable a built-in response policy to automatically terminate processes exhibiting behaviors typical of PHP2Shell exploitation:
Notably, Gemini 4 Argon made an invaluable contribution to finding the vulnerability, exploit development, attack detection, and validation of the patch.

Wiz customers should refer to the Wiz Threat Intel Center advisory for PHP2Shell , which includes built-in coverage for agentless and runtime vulnerability detection, exploitation detection via Wiz Defend and Sensor, and automatic response policies, alongside remediation and threat hunting guidance.

These vulnerabilities include memory disclosure and unauthenticated remote code execution in PHP itself, independent of the application running on top of it , putting every affected website in immediate risk.
Every PHP version released in the last decade is affected by at least one of these vulnerabilities, going back to version 5.4.

We combined these vulnerabilities into a single exploit script, php2shell, and demonstrated that it could execute code remotely without authentication on deployments of WordPress ( wordpress:latest ), Drupal ( drupal:latest ), and Joomla ( joomla:latest ), using their latest container images at the time of testing.
Wiz researchers will walk through what we've discovered, how we found these vulnerabilities, and what security teams need to know to assess their exposure and respond.

extraction.body: Core PHP engine flaws enable remote code execution and Heartbleed-style memory disclosure across the web. Wiz Research uncovered multiple critical vulnerabilities in core PHP, a popular general-purpose scripting language that powers 70% of all websites in the world. Successful exploitation could allow attackers to take control of affected servers, steal sensitive data, and deface the websites running on them. PHP is a backbone of the web: it’s the programming language powering WordPress, Joomla, Drupal, Wikipedia’s MediaWiki, and many others. These vulnerabilities include memory disclosure and unauthenticated remote code execution in PHP itself, independent of the application running on top of it , putting every affected website in immediate risk. Every PHP version released in the last decade is affected by at least one of these vulnerabilities, going back to version 5.4. Attackers can exploit them remotely, in some cases fairly easily. Immediate patching is strongly advised. On October 21, 2026, PHP released the patch fixing multiple memory-safety vulnerabilities in the core engine. These findings rank among the most severe vulnerabilities discovered in PHP, and arguably in software history. The underlying flaws had been present for decades, but demonstrating their exploitability required an exceptionally complex chain of steps, at the edge of what human researchers could practically achieve. Frontier AI models substantially reduced that barrier, turning a longstanding flaw into an exploit. In this post, we explain how frontier AI helped us find and fix vulnerabilities that had remained hidden in the PHP codebase for more than a decade. The issues described below all stem from key architecture decisions, some made over a decade ago, and were grouped under two CVEs, with severity reaching CVSS 9.2. The work grew into a cross-industry effort to protect customers, find variants, deploy detections and mitigations, and verify a patch in time for coordinated disclosure. Nearly every PHP version is affected by at least one of these issues, including releases dating back to PHP 5.4. The vulnerabilities can allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code on affected servers or read sensitive process memory. That memory may contain passwords, authentication tokens, API keys and certificates belonging to other requests or the server itself. PHP is the programming language behind much of the web, powering WordPress, Drupal and MediaWiki, the software that runs Wikipedia. A flaw in its core engine can affect websites across this ecosystem, even when their own application code is secure. Some vulnerabilities become turning points because they challenge fundamental assumptions about security. In 2014, Heartbleed exposed the fragility of shared infrastructure securing the internet. In 2021, Log4Shell revealed how deeply embedded software dependencies could create widespread exposure that organizations struggled to identify. We believe PHP2Shell could mark a similar turning point for the AI era, illustrating how AI can change the practical exploitability of longstanding vulnerabilities. Building the exploit required chaining multiple flaws and adapting to each target’s memory layout through repeated testing and debugging. Frontier models were critical to making this process practical, enabling us to develop and adapt working exploits across multiple applications in hours. As the time and expertise required for this work decrease, complexity may no longer provide a meaningful barrier, changing how we define what is vulnerable in practice. Wiz Research would like to thank the PHP team, Calif and OpenAI for their work on discovery, coordination and patch verification. OpenAI and Calif also published blogs containing details on the vulnerability – its history, technical details, and insight into the disclosure process. PHP posted as well. We’d also like to express our sincere gratitude towards Automattic, Akamai, AWS, Cloudflare , Fastly, Google , Imperva, Microsoft, Vercel, and many others, for helping prepare guidance and out-of-the-box mitigations for customers who cannot apply the patch immediately. All of the disclosed vulnerabilities are memory-safety issues that stem from bugs in how PHP handles fatal errors while processing requests, particularly out-of-memory errors. These bugs can leave a corrupted internal PHP state behind after a request ends unexpectedly. A later request or worker can reuse that stale state, leading to memory disclosure or corruption. Below you can find a table that demonstrates what type of impact was demonstrated by each of the bugs we reported to PHP. The applications listed below are targets we chose for the RCE demonstrations. They are representative targets - exploitation does not require one of these CMSs, as the vulnerable code is in PHP itself. While this blog covers only four instances of exploitable bugs (grouped under two CVEs) that follow this problematic pattern, there are other tracked, and likely untracked, variants of this issue in the PHP codebase. These variants have different requirements for exploitation and can lead to different types of impact. In any case, the patch provided by the PHP team fixes the issue at its core and eliminates all variants in the patched release. We combined these vulnerabilities into a single exploit script, php2shell, and demonstrated that it could execute code remotely without authentication on deployments of WordPress ( wordpress:latest ), Drupal ( drupal:latest ), and Joomla ( joomla:latest ), using their latest container images at the time of testing. These platforms illustrate the impact, but the vulnerabilities are in PHP itself. Exploitation does not depend on a flaw in the application’s code: even a simple “Hello World” application running on an affected PHP version can be vulnerable. Separately, we demonstrated that attackers could read sensitive data from the PHP process’s memory, including passwords, tokens, and API keys, without needing to achieve remote code execution. Demonstrations of PHP2Shell with Wordpress, Joomla, and Drupal: We used Wiz Atlas , Gemini 4 Argon and GPT-5.6 Sol throughout this research. Notably, Gemini 4 Argon made an invaluable contribution to finding the vulnerability, exploit development, attack detection, and validation of the patch. Using Gemini 4 Argon, the team at Wiz has shown why frontier AI is a game-changer for cyber defense. For over a decade, these critical vulnerabilities remained unaddressed because vulnerability discovery and exploitation were incredibly complex. We're pleased to see Gemini 4 Argon help defenders bridge that gap, finding vulnerabilities and helping patch them. Prior to public disclosure, Wiz Research worked with the PHP team, Calif and OpenAI on discovery, coordination and patch verification. passages: Core PHP engine flaws enable remote code execution and Heartbleed-style memory disclosure across the web.

Wiz Research uncovered multiple critical vulnerabilities in core PHP, a popular general-purpose scripting language that powers 70% of all websites in the world. Successful exploitation could allow attackers to take control of affected servers, steal sensitive data, and deface the websites running on them.
PHP is a backbone of the web: it’s the programming language powering WordPress, Joomla, Drupal, Wikipedia’s MediaWiki, and many others.

These vulnerabilities include memory disclosure and unauthenticated remote code execution in PHP itself, independent of the application running on top of it , putting every affected website in immediate risk.

Every PHP version released in the last decade is affected by at least one of these vulnerabilities, going back to version 5.4. Attackers can exploit them remotely, in some cases fairly easily. Immediate patching is strongly advised.
On October 21, 2026, PHP released the patch fixing multiple memory-safety vulnerabilities in the core engine.

These findings rank among the most severe vulnerabilities discovered in PHP, and arguably in software history. The underlying flaws had been present for decades, but demonstrating their exploitability required an exceptionally complex chain of steps, at the edge of what human researchers could practically achieve. Frontier AI models substantially reduced that barrier, turning a longstanding flaw into an exploit.

In this post, we explain how frontier AI helped us find and fix vulnerabilities that had remained hidden in the PHP codebase for more than a decade. The issues described below all stem from key architecture decisions, some made over a decade ago, and were grouped under two CVEs, with severity reaching CVSS 9.2. The work grew into a cross-industry effort to protect customers, find variants, deploy detections and mitigations, and verify a patch in time for coordinated disclosure.

Nearly every PHP version is affected by at least one of these issues, including releases dating back to PHP 5.4. The vulnerabilities can allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code on affected servers or read sensitive process memory. That memory may contain passwords, authentication tokens, API keys and certificates belonging to other requests or the server itself.

PHP is the programming language behind much of the web, powering WordPress, Drupal and MediaWiki, the software that runs Wikipedia. A flaw in its core engine can affect websites across this ecosystem, even when their own application code is secure.

Some vulnerabilities become turning points because they challenge fundamental assumptions about security. In 2014, Heartbleed exposed the fragility of shared infrastructure securing the internet. In 2021, Log4Shell revealed how deeply embedded software dependencies could create widespread exposure that organizations struggled to identify. We believe PHP2Shell could mark a similar turning point for the AI era, illustrating how AI can change the practical exploitability of longstanding vulnerabilities. Building the exploit required chaining multiple flaws and adapting to each target’s memory layout through repeated testing and debugging. Frontier models were critical to making this process practical, enabling us to develop and adapt working exploits across multiple applications in hours. As the time and expertise required for this work decrease, complexity may no longer provide a meaningful barrier, changing how we define what is vulnerable in practice.

Wiz Research would like to thank the PHP team, Calif and OpenAI for their work on discovery, coordination and patch verification. OpenAI and Calif also published blogs containing details on the vulnerability – its history, technical details, and insight into the disclosure process. PHP posted as well.

We’d also like to express our sincere gratitude towards Automattic, Akamai, AWS, Cloudflare , Fastly, Google , Imperva, Microsoft, Vercel, and many others, for helping prepare guidance and out-of-the-box mitigations for customers who cannot apply the patch immediately.

All of the disclosed vulnerabilities are memory-safety issues that stem from bugs in how PHP handles fatal errors while processing requests, particularly out-of-memory errors. These bugs can leave a corrupted internal PHP state behind after a request ends unexpectedly. A later request or worker can reuse that stale state, leading to memory disclosure or corruption.

Below you can find a table that demonstrates what type of impact was demonstrated by each of the bugs we reported to PHP. The applications listed below are targets we chose for the RCE demonstrations. They are representative targets - exploitation does not require one of these CMSs, as the vulnerable code is in PHP itself.

While this blog covers only four instances of exploitable bugs (grouped under two CVEs) that follow this problematic pattern, there are other tracked, and likely untracked, variants of this issue in the PHP codebase. These variants have different requirements for exploitation and can lead to different types of impact. In any case, the patch provided by the PHP team fixes the issue at its core and eliminates all variants in the patched release.

We combined these vulnerabilities into a single exploit script, php2shell, and demonstrated that it could execute code remotely without authentication on deployments of WordPress ( wordpress:latest ), Drupal ( drupal:latest ), and Joomla ( joomla:latest ), using their latest container images at the time of testing.

These platforms illustrate the impact, but the vulnerabilities are in PHP itself. Exploitation does not depend on a flaw in the application’s code: even a simple “Hello World” application running on an affected PHP version can be vulnerable.
Separately, we demonstrated that attackers could read sensitive data from the PHP process’s memory, including passwords, tokens, and API keys, without needing to achieve remote code execution.

PHP's security advisory says "all PHP installations serving web requests" are at risk, including PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed. PHP considers the risk "highest for mod_php, with a demonstrated exploit where an unauthenticated request can trigger the attack before any application code runs." PHP says "There are no complete mitigations, updating is the only safe choice." PHP powers many websites and web applications, including content management systems, e-commerce platforms and custom web services (BleepingComputer), so it is very likely to be somewhere in your vendors' stacks. PHP describes the two flaws as follows (php.net security advisory and GitHub advisories): Both have the CVSS v4.0 vector AV:N/AC:H/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N (score 9.2) from PHP as CNA. For CVE-2026-109618, PHP says complete remote code execution "was validated over HTTP against mod_php", and that source analysis supports PHP-FPM as susceptible, "though no complete FPM exploit has been demonstrated". For CVE-2026-109619, PHP says "Session lifecycle RCE was validated against mod_php and FPM"; it adds that the FPM path "depends on a suitable application operation" ( GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp ). This advisory does not cover how to exploit the flaws. PHP's CVE records credit Ryan at Calif.io, Wiz and OpenAI with reporting or finding the flaws, and PHP developers Arnaud Le Blanc, Ilija Tovilo, Jakub Zelenka and Nora Dossche with the fix. CVE / KEV status (checked 21 Oct 2026, 17:29 Cyprus time): Both CVEs are published on cve.org by PHP. NVD lists both as "Received" and shows only PHP's CNA score (CVSS v4.0 9.2, Critical). NVD has not published its own score. Neither CVE is in CISA's KEV catalog (catalog version 2026.10.20, released 20 Oct 2026). None published. PHP, CERT-EU and the NCSC have released no indicators of compromise. Cloudflare says it was seeing early attacks before the release but has not published details. Rescana has not confirmed in-the-wild exploitation, and neither CVE is in CISA's KEV catalog as of this update. The fix is now out, but you are only protected once every vendor running PHP in its stack has deployed it, and many of those dependencies are invisible from the outside. The fixes are in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35, and the team is strongly urging all PHP users to update immediately. “These findings rank among the most severe vulnerabilities discovered in PHP, and arguably in software history. The underlying flaws had been present for decades, but demonstrating their exploitability required an exceptionally complex chain of steps, at the edge of what human researchers could practically achieve. Frontier AI models substantially reduced that barrier, turning a longstanding flaw into an exploit,” Wiz researchers explained . Every PHP installation that serves web requests is affected, including PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed. Setups using mod_php face the greatest danger. A working exploit has already shown that a single unauthenticated request can trigger the attack before any application code runs. “The PHP situation will lead to a mass of incidents – it’s one of the biggest vulns in years,” noted security researcher Kevin Beaumont. CVE-2026-109618 – RCE via OOM corruption : out-of-memory handling can interrupt PHP while internal request data is only partially initialized. Request cleanup may then treat the invalid data as valid. CVE-2026-109619 – RCE via stale global state : request-owned internal state can survive after its backing memory has been freed. A later request handled by the same worker may use that stale state before normal initialization resets it. The UK’s National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) is urging organizations to consider taking offline any system that can’t be fixed right away. “So many embedded installations out there that will never be patched. Too many forgotten, unmaintained apps. There will be a long tail for this one,” commented computer forensics expert Hal Pomeranz. Update to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35. Downloads are available here . Linux distributions and long-term support (LTS) vendors got the patches ahead of the public release, so admins should check with their vendor for updated packages. Anyone who relies on rpms.remirepo.net , a volunteer-maintained repository, is advised to switch to distribution packages or build PHP from source so they can patch immediately. The repository will not have updates available today. Because the vulnerabilities are so severe, the PHP security team has also released minimal source backports for PHP 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1. These are meant for people who build from source or who don’t have an LTS vendor. “PHP sites behind Cloudflare already have an initial set of WAF rules deployed for the known exploit vectors in these vulnerabilities. The rules are available to all customers, including free,” said Dane Knecht, CTO at Cloudflare.

sources.title: Two Critical PHP Vulnerabilities: Security Release Due 21 October 2026, Prepare Now - Rescana
passages: Update (21 Oct 2026): PHP has shipped its security release.
PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 fix the two vulnerabilities, which PHP now confirms are CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 .
PHP's CNA rates both CVSS v4.0 9.2 (Critical) .
PHP says "updating is the only safe choice" ( PHP security advisory ).
PHP has released fixes for two critical vulnerabilities that can allow unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE) on servers that run PHP to serve web requests.
PHP's GitHub security advisories were published at 13:34 UTC (16:34 Cyprus time), ahead of the scheduled 14:00 UTC release time.
Neither CVE is in CISA's KEV catalog (catalog version 2026.10.20, released 20 Oct 2026).
PHP, CERT-EU and the NCSC have released no indicators of compromise.
Cloudflare says it was seeing early attacks before the release but has not published details.
This advisory does not cover how to exploit the flaws.

PHP's security advisory says "all PHP installations serving web requests" are at risk, including PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed. PHP considers the risk "highest for mod_php, with a demonstrated exploit where an unauthenticated request can trigger the attack before any application code runs." PHP says "There are no complete mitigations, updating is the only safe choice." For CVE-2026-109619, PHP says "Session lifecycle RCE was validated against mod_php and FPM"; it adds that the FPM path "depends on a suitable application operation" ( GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp ). This advisory does not cover how to exploit the flaws. extraction.body: Tech > Computing > Gadgets > VR/AR Productivity Exclusive: Supernatural is relaunching in early access and could expand beyond Meta Quest headsets. Meanwhile, Meta VR Glasses could shape what comes next for fitness. I was heartbroken earlier this year when Supernatural , my favorite VR fitness app on Meta Quest, shut down . But now it’s making a comeback as an indie company. The new app returns this week in early access, with all the same trainers and a focus on getting the classic experience going again. But the funny thing is, just as it’s returning, the very nature of VR is starting to change. Meta’s VR Glasses , coming next spring, promise to shrink down the future of Meta’s headsets to glasses-like form. And Supernatural’s team feels confident that slimmer, lighter hardware will be an excellent fit for fitness. If so, it could be the beginning of something new. More glasses-like devices on the horizon, including Meta VR Glasses, Google’s Xreal Aura and even Snap Specs , could enable virtual fitness experiences — and everything else VR has promised — in more portable forms that trap less sweat. But in the meantime, I’m glad the app’s back for Quest. “We’re coming back because people raised their voices and started petitions and said we need this to be part of our lives. We wouldn’t be doing this if that hadn’t happened,” Leanne Pedante, Supernatural’s head of fitness and one of its in-game coaches, said to me of the new, smaller Supernatural team. I talked to Pedante and James Senior, Supernatural Health’s CEO, about the new service and what else could be coming once Meta VR Glasses roll around next year. The early-access version of the new Supernatural app — which will once again launch on Quest headsets — will gradually bring back the trainers and music tracks from the Meta-owned version. There will be thousands of workouts, and new 3D environments as well. But the concept behind Supernatural, a rhythm-based set of song-driven choreographed game-like workouts with actual human coaches that talk alongside you, remains the same. “That coaching you hear is coming out of a person who is physically experiencing the same thing that you are in the moment,” said Pedante, who feels that’s a key ingredient versus opting for an AI companion. “That creates this kind of invisible empathy — the coach is able to anticipate what you need to hear or what your body is probably doing.” Those 3D landscapes were always one of the most compelling parts of Supernatural, but so were the trainers, who appear in 3D volumetric video before workouts and speak in your ears as you punch and swing to each song. I developed an emotional connection to my workout progress. The songs are being relicensed, according to Senior, but many familiar tracks are coming back, along with new ones. New workouts and content will follow soon after. “The music deals have really accelerated in the last three weeks,” he said. “We’re pretty much going to have the full catalog back that people have in the old service, and in the coming weeks, we’ll also be bringing back tracks that had disappeared from the Meta service over the last 12-18 months because of licensing restrictions.” The original workouts have also been remastered for the new app, with better-synchronized beat mapping across existing Quest headsets. “Each has different components, which very subtly causes clock drift once it reaches the application layer in the platform. In the new app, we’ve built in new logic to account for that,” Senior added. Senior also told me there’s a special comeback workout in which some of the trainers share their emotional journeys through leaving Meta and going independent, with songs chosen to fit their moods. He mentioned Good Feeling by Flo Rida, Celebration by Kool and the Gang and We are Family by Sister Sledge as some of the tracks. But the price is going up to $200 a year, or $20 a month. Original “founding member” Supernatural users will get a $20 discount on the annual plan. It looks like a lot of the previous features will be part of the package, too: Fitness history and achievements will come over, and although the new experience has a new companion phone app, it’ll still work for tracking heart rate during workouts. That’s another key part of what made Supernatural actually feel like a real fitness tool for me. But that app and the heart rate tracking aren’t available now. They’re coming later this year. One big change down the road will be support for hand tracking. For now, the new Supernatural app still uses controllers to track hand movements during workouts. There’s a good reason for the shift: Meta’s VR Glasses, coming next year, won’t include controllers in the box. The next wave of VR could make hand tracking the default. Supernatural’s team feels confident that hand tracking is now good enough to step in as a replacement — but also that Meta VR Glasses will be a way for Supernatural and other fitness apps to take a leap forward. Meta’s upcoming $1,299 VR Glasses have a completely different design from Quest headsets: a glasses-like form with a tethered, phone-sized processing puck. In a promo image for the new Supernatural, Pedante even poses with Meta VR Glasses. It’s a nod to where the Supernatural team thinks VR fitness is heading. Pedante and Senior see Meta VR Glasses as a perfect fit for where things are going for immersive fitness. “It’s a lightweight device that’s highly breathable. It’s not susceptible to fogging. It has high definition and, frankly, it’s a device that’s perfect for the fitness use case,” says Senior, who previously worked at Meta on VR platforms. It’s a bold claim. Until now, there hasn’t been a smaller-scale VR device that’s workout-capable. When I wore Meta’s VR Glasses last month, I wondered how well they’d be able to run apps such as Supernatural. Meta has already confirmed that fit accessories are coming for its VR glasses that could also make them easier to wear during activities such as workouts. Supernatural’s team is now independent and no longer tied exclusively to Meta. That opens the door to other platforms, although the VR landscape isn’t as big as it once was. SteamVR could be a possibility. So could Android XR. And perhaps even platforms that aren’t VR at all. Senior confirmed that for now, Supernatural is still just a Meta app, but other devices are being looked at. I wonder about glasses-like hardware, such as Google’s imminent Xreal Aura or even Snap Specs . An app for Steam VR would be a big step, too. “It’s this interesting, convergent zone of AR and VR,” Senior said of the Aura glasses, which feel a bit like VR and use different display technology from Meta’s VR Glasses, but a similar processing puck. “That’s an area we would want to experiment and lean in,” he said without committing to whether it might emerge there, too. Clearly, Supernatural is aiming to be a killer app for Meta’s VR Glasses, and Senior said some of the headset’s features — higher-res displays and eye tracking — might also be incorporated into the experience. I’m just excited to dive back in. As Supernatural followed its strange 2026 arc from being cast out of Meta to becoming a key app for Meta once again, I fell out of my own VR workout routine. But I’ll be putting the headset on again, and I’ll let you know what it feels like when I do. © 2026 CNET, a Ziff Davis company. All rights reserved.
