Exclusive: Supernatural is relaunching in early access and could expand beyond Meta Quest headsets. Meanwhile, Meta VR Glasses could shape what comes next for fitness.

I was heartbroken earlier this year when Supernatural , my favorite VR fitness app on Meta Quest, shut down . But now it’s making a comeback as an indie company. The new app returns this week in early access, with all the same trainers and a focus on getting the classic experience going again. But the funny thing is, just as it’s returning, the very nature of VR is starting to change.

Meta’s VR Glasses , coming next spring, promise to shrink down the future of Meta’s headsets to glasses-like form. And Supernatural’s team feels confident that slimmer, lighter hardware will be an excellent fit for fitness. If so, it could be the beginning of something new. More glasses-like devices on the horizon, including Meta VR Glasses, Google’s Xreal Aura and even Snap Specs , could enable virtual fitness experiences — and everything else VR has promised — in more portable forms that trap less sweat.

But in the meantime, I’m glad the app’s back for Quest. “We’re coming back because people raised their voices and started petitions and said we need this to be part of our lives. We wouldn’t be doing this if that hadn’t happened,” Leanne Pedante, Supernatural’s head of fitness and one of its in-game coaches, said to me of the new, smaller Supernatural team.
I talked to Pedante and James Senior, Supernatural Health’s CEO, about the new service and what else could be coming once Meta VR Glasses roll around next year.

The early-access version of the new Supernatural app — which will once again launch on Quest headsets — will gradually bring back the trainers and music tracks from the Meta-owned version. There will be thousands of workouts, and new 3D environments as well.
But the concept behind Supernatural, a rhythm-based set of song-driven choreographed game-like workouts with actual human coaches that talk alongside you, remains the same.

“That coaching you hear is coming out of a person who is physically experiencing the same thing that you are in the moment,” said Pedante, who feels that’s a key ingredient versus opting for an AI companion. “That creates this kind of invisible empathy — the coach is able to anticipate what you need to hear or what your body is probably doing.”

Those 3D landscapes were always one of the most compelling parts of Supernatural, but so were the trainers, who appear in 3D volumetric video before workouts and speak in your ears as you punch and swing to each song. I developed an emotional connection to my workout progress.
The songs are being relicensed, according to Senior, but many familiar tracks are coming back, along with new ones. New workouts and content will follow soon after.

“The music deals have really accelerated in the last three weeks,” he said. “We’re pretty much going to have the full catalog back that people have in the old service, and in the coming weeks, we’ll also be bringing back tracks that had disappeared from the Meta service over the last 12-18 months because of licensing restrictions.”

The original workouts have also been remastered for the new app, with better-synchronized beat mapping across existing Quest headsets. “Each has different components, which very subtly causes clock drift once it reaches the application layer in the platform. In the new app, we’ve built in new logic to account for that,” Senior added.

Senior also told me there’s a special comeback workout in which some of the trainers share their emotional journeys through leaving Meta and going independent, with songs chosen to fit their moods. He mentioned Good Feeling by Flo Rida, Celebration by Kool and the Gang and We are Family by Sister Sledge as some of the tracks.
But the price is going up to $200 a year, or $20 a month. Original “founding member” Supernatural users will get a $20 discount on the annual plan.

It looks like a lot of the previous features will be part of the package, too: Fitness history and achievements will come over, and although the new experience has a new companion phone app, it’ll still work for tracking heart rate during workouts. That’s another key part of what made Supernatural actually feel like a real fitness tool for me. But that app and the heart rate tracking aren’t available now. They’re coming later this year.

One big change down the road will be support for hand tracking. For now, the new Supernatural app still uses controllers to track hand movements during workouts. There’s a good reason for the shift: Meta’s VR Glasses, coming next year, won’t include controllers in the box. The next wave of VR could make hand tracking the default.

Supernatural’s team feels confident that hand tracking is now good enough to step in as a replacement — but also that Meta VR Glasses will be a way for Supernatural and other fitness apps to take a leap forward.
Meta’s upcoming $1,299 VR Glasses have a completely different design from Quest headsets: a glasses-like form with a tethered, phone-sized processing puck.

In a promo image for the new Supernatural, Pedante even poses with Meta VR Glasses. It’s a nod to where the Supernatural team thinks VR fitness is heading. Pedante and Senior see Meta VR Glasses as a perfect fit for where things are going for immersive fitness.

“It’s a lightweight device that’s highly breathable. It’s not susceptible to fogging. It has high definition and, frankly, it’s a device that’s perfect for the fitness use case,” says Senior, who previously worked at Meta on VR platforms.

It’s a bold claim. Until now, there hasn’t been a smaller-scale VR device that’s workout-capable. When I wore Meta’s VR Glasses last month, I wondered how well they’d be able to run apps such as Supernatural. Meta has already confirmed that fit accessories are coming for its VR glasses that could also make them easier to wear during activities such as workouts.

Supernatural’s team is now independent and no longer tied exclusively to Meta. That opens the door to other platforms, although the VR landscape isn’t as big as it once was. SteamVR could be a possibility. So could Android XR. And perhaps even platforms that aren’t VR at all.

Senior confirmed that for now, Supernatural is still just a Meta app, but other devices are being looked at. I wonder about glasses-like hardware, such as Google’s imminent Xreal Aura or even Snap Specs . An app for Steam VR would be a big step, too.

“It’s this interesting, convergent zone of AR and VR,” Senior said of the Aura glasses, which feel a bit like VR and use different display technology from Meta’s VR Glasses, but a similar processing puck. “That’s an area we would want to experiment and lean in,” he said without committing to whether it might emerge there, too.

Clearly, Supernatural is aiming to be a killer app for Meta’s VR Glasses, and Senior said some of the headset’s features — higher-res displays and eye tracking — might also be incorporated into the experience.

I’m just excited to dive back in. As Supernatural followed its strange 2026 arc from being cast out of Meta to becoming a key app for Meta once again, I fell out of my own VR workout routine. But I’ll be putting the headset on again, and I’ll let you know what it feels like when I do.

sources.title: Meta killed its most popular workout app, but Supernatural is coming back, and this time Meta isn't in charge - Android Central
passages: As you probably guessed, one of those studios was Within, the house that made Supernatural and was acquired by Meta (then Facebook) back in 2021 .

Despite a landmark legal battle between the FTC and Meta over the acquisition , Meta washed its hands of what it used to claim was "the future of at-home workouts." But because of a thriving, outspoken online community, Supernatural is coming back, and this time it's fully free of Meta's clutches.

Regardless of the specifics, one thing is certain: Supernatural is back, the community is on fire for the new direction of its favorite workout app, and VR fitness is about to have a full-on renaissance this fall.
The real question is whether other now-defunct Meta studios will also see this kind of revival, as well.
It's because Supernatural wasn't just an excellent, coach-led daily workout.
It was an entire community of people who found a way to make working out fun and share in those wins together.
They won with each other, and the unceremonious plug-pulling that Meta did in January 2026 was more than just heartbreaking to those folks.
It was the end of something that changed their lives for the better.

Per the official Supernatural website , your favorite coaches will be back "on day one," new workouts and future features will be built using feedback, and the community will be central to the entire experience.

Since the coaches need to be paid for their ongoing work, Supernatural will still be a subscription-only experience, but fans can lock in a "founder's rate" by registering interest in the relaunch , which is currently slated for the fall of 2026.
Each day brought a new coach-led workout, filled with popular music, gorgeous vistas, and gameplay that rewarded those who put in 100% effort.
As Russell Holly put it when he wrote about it that May , "I'm dripping in sweat, every inch of me is sore, and I have a huge smile on my face."

"We’re returning to our roots and plan to build major parts of the technology from the ground up as a much smaller company," says the Supernatural team, and that tells me that this game will almost certainly be less reliant on Meta's proprietary development tools and, instead, built in a way that's more sustainable for future growth.
The team isn't shying away from saying that this isn't the same old app under new management.
It's OG management taking back the reins and creating something new (and hopefully better) in the process.

Supernatural's original April 2020 launch couldn't have been more timely.
Most of the world had shut down due to COVID.

People weren't leaving their homes, weren't going to work, and definitely weren't going to the gym, but Supernatural quickly paved the way for people to stay fit at home and still get that coach-led experience they'd been sorely missing.
My genuine first impression is pictured above, and it tells you everything you need to know.

Supernatural's huge online community spoke up, and the original founders are back with a whole new vision of VR fitness.

The news sideswiped me mid-morning on Wednesday when the Facebook community's post (via Good Virtual Reality ) was published, and it's the biggest VR news to hit since Meta closed most of its internal studios back in January.
There's no chance the core gameplay loop changes, although I imagine plenty of new ideas from the community can be implemented in this rebuilt Supernatural.

coreStoryFacts.text: The game’s developers also write, “More back-catalog favorites will return in the weeks and months ahead, with new music, higher-definition destinations and new features on the way.” Other new features coming later include the return of Supernatural Together, which has been “rebuilt from the ground up.” Supernatural is also getting a mobile companion app it says members can use to “Track progress and heart rate and stay connected beyond the headset.” Supernatural says people who played the original version of the game “can transfer their points, start date, streaks, favorites and badges” to the new version through December 3rd.
Starting next week, Supernatural will get new workouts every week.
It’s also offering rewards for “founding members,” starting with a custom bat, with more coming throughout early access.

Despite Meta saying it would stop creating new content for Supernatural, the beloved fitness VR game is back after spinning off to go its own way and is relaunching with an Early Access preview in the Meta Horizon Store.
I was heartbroken earlier this year when Supernatural , my favorite VR fitness app on Meta Quest, shut down .
But the funny thing is, just as it’s returning, the very nature of VR is starting to change.
“We’re coming back because people raised their voices and started petitions and said we need this to be part of our lives.
We wouldn’t be doing this if that hadn’t happened,” Leanne Pedante, Supernatural’s head of fitness and one of its in-game coaches, said to me of the new, smaller Supernatural team.

And Supernatural’s team feels confident that slimmer, lighter hardware will be an excellent fit for fitness.

“The music deals have really accelerated in the last three weeks,” he said. “We’re pretty much going to have the full catalog back that people have in the old service, and in the coming weeks, we’ll also be bringing back tracks that had disappeared from the Meta service over the last 12-18 months because of licensing restrictions.”
It’s a nod to where the Supernatural team thinks VR fitness is heading.
As Supernatural followed its strange 2026 arc from being cast out of Meta to becoming a key app for Meta once again, I fell out of my own VR workout routine.

extraction.body: Tech > Computing > Gadgets > VR/AR Productivity Exclusive: Supernatural is relaunching in early access and could expand beyond Meta Quest headsets. Meanwhile, Meta VR Glasses could shape what comes next for fitness. I was heartbroken earlier this year when Supernatural , my favorite VR fitness app on Meta Quest, shut down . But now it’s making a comeback as an indie company. The new app returns this week in early access, with all the same trainers and a focus on getting the classic experience going again. But the funny thing is, just as it’s returning, the very nature of VR is starting to change. Meta’s VR Glasses , coming next spring, promise to shrink down the future of Meta’s headsets to glasses-like form. And Supernatural’s team feels confident that slimmer, lighter hardware will be an excellent fit for fitness. If so, it could be the beginning of something new. More glasses-like devices on the horizon, including Meta VR Glasses, Google’s Xreal Aura and even Snap Specs , could enable virtual fitness experiences — and everything else VR has promised — in more portable forms that trap less sweat. But in the meantime, I’m glad the app’s back for Quest. “We’re coming back because people raised their voices and started petitions and said we need this to be part of our lives. We wouldn’t be doing this if that hadn’t happened,” Leanne Pedante, Supernatural’s head of fitness and one of its in-game coaches, said to me of the new, smaller Supernatural team. I talked to Pedante and James Senior, Supernatural Health’s CEO, about the new service and what else could be coming once Meta VR Glasses roll around next year. The early-access version of the new Supernatural app — which will once again launch on Quest headsets — will gradually bring back the trainers and music tracks from the Meta-owned version. There will be thousands of workouts, and new 3D environments as well. But the concept behind Supernatural, a rhythm-based set of song-driven choreographed game-like workouts with actual human coaches that talk alongside you, remains the same. “That coaching you hear is coming out of a person who is physically experiencing the same thing that you are in the moment,” said Pedante, who feels that’s a key ingredient versus opting for an AI companion. “That creates this kind of invisible empathy — the coach is able to anticipate what you need to hear or what your body is probably doing.” Those 3D landscapes were always one of the most compelling parts of Supernatural, but so were the trainers, who appear in 3D volumetric video before workouts and speak in your ears as you punch and swing to each song. I developed an emotional connection to my workout progress. The songs are being relicensed, according to Senior, but many familiar tracks are coming back, along with new ones. New workouts and content will follow soon after. “The music deals have really accelerated in the last three weeks,” he said. “We’re pretty much going to have the full catalog back that people have in the old service, and in the coming weeks, we’ll also be bringing back tracks that had disappeared from the Meta service over the last 12-18 months because of licensing restrictions.” The original workouts have also been remastered for the new app, with better-synchronized beat mapping across existing Quest headsets. “Each has different components, which very subtly causes clock drift once it reaches the application layer in the platform. In the new app, we’ve built in new logic to account for that,” Senior added. Senior also told me there’s a special comeback workout in which some of the trainers share their emotional journeys through leaving Meta and going independent, with songs chosen to fit their moods. He mentioned Good Feeling by Flo Rida, Celebration by Kool and the Gang and We are Family by Sister Sledge as some of the tracks. But the price is going up to $200 a year, or $20 a month. Original “founding member” Supernatural users will get a $20 discount on the annual plan. It looks like a lot of the previous features will be part of the package, too: Fitness history and achievements will come over, and although the new experience has a new companion phone app, it’ll still work for tracking heart rate during workouts. That’s another key part of what made Supernatural actually feel like a real fitness tool for me. But that app and the heart rate tracking aren’t available now. They’re coming later this year. One big change down the road will be support for hand tracking. For now, the new Supernatural app still uses controllers to track hand movements during workouts. There’s a good reason for the shift: Meta’s VR Glasses, coming next year, won’t include controllers in the box. The next wave of VR could make hand tracking the default. Supernatural’s team feels confident that hand tracking is now good enough to step in as a replacement — but also that Meta VR Glasses will be a way for Supernatural and other fitness apps to take a leap forward. Meta’s upcoming $1,299 VR Glasses have a completely different design from Quest headsets: a glasses-like form with a tethered, phone-sized processing puck. In a promo image for the new Supernatural, Pedante even poses with Meta VR Glasses. It’s a nod to where the Supernatural team thinks VR fitness is heading. Pedante and Senior see Meta VR Glasses as a perfect fit for where things are going for immersive fitness. “It’s a lightweight device that’s highly breathable. It’s not susceptible to fogging. It has high definition and, frankly, it’s a device that’s perfect for the fitness use case,” says Senior, who previously worked at Meta on VR platforms. It’s a bold claim. Until now, there hasn’t been a smaller-scale VR device that’s workout-capable. When I wore Meta’s VR Glasses last month, I wondered how well they’d be able to run apps such as Supernatural. Meta has already confirmed that fit accessories are coming for its VR glasses that could also make them easier to wear during activities such as workouts. Supernatural’s team is now independent and no longer tied exclusively to Meta. That opens the door to other platforms, although the VR landscape isn’t as big as it once was. SteamVR could be a possibility. So could Android XR. And perhaps even platforms that aren’t VR at all. Senior confirmed that for now, Supernatural is still just a Meta app, but other devices are being looked at. I wonder about glasses-like hardware, such as Google’s imminent Xreal Aura or even Snap Specs . An app for Steam VR would be a big step, too. “It’s this interesting, convergent zone of AR and VR,” Senior said of the Aura glasses, which feel a bit like VR and use different display technology from Meta’s VR Glasses, but a similar processing puck. “That’s an area we would want to experiment and lean in,” he said without committing to whether it might emerge there, too. Clearly, Supernatural is aiming to be a killer app for Meta’s VR Glasses, and Senior said some of the headset’s features — higher-res displays and eye tracking — might also be incorporated into the experience. I’m just excited to dive back in. As Supernatural followed its strange 2026 arc from being cast out of Meta to becoming a key app for Meta once again, I fell out of my own VR workout routine. But I’ll be putting the headset on again, and I’ll let you know what it feels like when I do. © 2026 CNET, a Ziff Davis company. All rights reserved.

When I wore Meta’s VR Glasses last month, I wondered how well they’d be able to run apps such as Supernatural. Meta has already confirmed that fit accessories are coming for its VR glasses that could also make them easier to wear during activities such as workouts.

Supernatural’s team is now independent and no longer tied exclusively to Meta. That opens the door to other platforms, although the VR landscape isn’t as big as it once was. SteamVR could be a possibility. So could Android XR. And perhaps even platforms that aren’t VR at all.

Senior confirmed that for now, Supernatural is still just a Meta app, but other devices are being looked at. I wonder about glasses-like hardware, such as Google’s imminent Xreal Aura or even Snap Specs . An app for Steam VR would be a big step, too.

“It’s this interesting, convergent zone of AR and VR,” Senior said of the Aura glasses, which feel a bit like VR and use different display technology from Meta’s VR Glasses, but a similar processing puck. “That’s an area we would want to experiment and lean in,” he said without committing to whether it might emerge there, too.

Clearly, Supernatural is aiming to be a killer app for Meta’s VR Glasses, and Senior said some of the headset’s features — higher-res displays and eye tracking — might also be incorporated into the experience.

I’m just excited to dive back in. As Supernatural followed its strange 2026 arc from being cast out of Meta to becoming a key app for Meta once again, I fell out of my own VR workout routine. But I’ll be putting the headset on again, and I’ll let you know what it feels like when I do.

sources.title: Meta killed its most popular workout app, but Supernatural is coming back, and this time Meta isn't in charge - Android Central
passages: As you probably guessed, one of those studios was Within, the house that made Supernatural and was acquired by Meta (then Facebook) back in 2021 .

Despite a landmark legal battle between the FTC and Meta over the acquisition , Meta washed its hands of what it used to claim was "the future of at-home workouts." But because of a thriving, outspoken online community, Supernatural is coming back, and this time it's fully free of Meta's clutches.

Regardless of the specifics, one thing is certain: Supernatural is back, the community is on fire for the new direction of its favorite workout app, and VR fitness is about to have a full-on renaissance this fall.
The real question is whether other now-defunct Meta studios will also see this kind of revival, as well.
It's because Supernatural wasn't just an excellent, coach-led daily workout.
It was an entire community of people who found a way to make working out fun and share in those wins together.
They won with each other, and the unceremonious plug-pulling that Meta did in January 2026 was more than just heartbreaking to those folks.
It was the end of something that changed their lives for the better.

Per the official Supernatural website , your favorite coaches will be back "on day one," new workouts and future features will be built using feedback, and the community will be central to the entire experience.

Since the coaches need to be paid for their ongoing work, Supernatural will still be a subscription-only experience, but fans can lock in a "founder's rate" by registering interest in the relaunch , which is currently slated for the fall of 2026.
Each day brought a new coach-led workout, filled with popular music, gorgeous vistas, and gameplay that rewarded those who put in 100% effort.
As Russell Holly put it when he wrote about it that May , "I'm dripping in sweat, every inch of me is sore, and I have a huge smile on my face."

"We’re returning to our roots and plan to build major parts of the technology from the ground up as a much smaller company," says the Supernatural team, and that tells me that this game will almost certainly be less reliant on Meta's proprietary development tools and, instead, built in a way that's more sustainable for future growth.
The team isn't shying away from saying that this isn't the same old app under new management.
It's OG management taking back the reins and creating something new (and hopefully better) in the process.

My genuine first impression is pictured above, and it tells you everything you need to know. Supernatural isn't (or wasn't) just a realistic-looking Beat Saber clone. The official Supernatural Facebook community has over 113,000 members, and the responses to this week's news have been overwhelmingly positive. "No! extraction.body: Washington, DC – Congresswoman Shontel Brown (OH-11) has introduced the Securing Elections from AI Deception Act , legislation to prohibit the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to deprive or defraud individuals of their right to vote and require disclaimers on AI-generated content. The legislation would be enforced by the Federal Trade Commission and applies to federal, state, and local campaign content. The Securing Elections from AI Deception Act is endorsed by the NAACP, the Lawyer’s Committee for Civil Rights Under Law, and NETWORK Lobby for Catholic Social Justice. The legislation has 30 cosponsors in the House. Bill text available here . This week, the New York Times reported that over $130 million in AI-generated ads have flooded the airwaves this election year. According to analysis by Wesleyan University, 69% of ads with AI content do not have disclaimers . Campaign ads featuring deceptive AI-generated have proliferated in recent years ( Wall Street Journal , Reuters , New York Times ), including ads featuring deepfake video and audio. In 2024, deepfake images of Trump with Black supporters spread online . In addition to deceiving voters, AI could also be used to spread false information regarding election information as a tactic to suppress voting rights. In 2020, robocalls targeting Black voters in Ohio spread deliberately false information relating to voting by mail procedures. AI technology has the potential to encourage similar efforts in the future and make them more persuasive. “This isn’t complicated: voters deserve to know that the campaign content they see and hear is real. We need labels on AI-generated election content and we need to hold accountable those who use AI to knowingly spread false information. Pairing the latest technology with old-school dirty tricks is a dangerous combination. I’m proud to introduce the Securing Elections from AI Deception Act and will continue to defend the voting rights of every American,” said Congresswoman Shontel Brown . “Artificial intelligence cannot become another tool for voter deception and suppression. Black communities have long been targeted by efforts to mislead, intimidate, and exclude voters, and new technology can make those tactics more sophisticated and harder to detect. The Securing Elections From AI Deception Act puts necessary guardrails in place to protect voters and our democracy. The NAACP applauds Congresswoman Brown for her continued leadership,” said Cedric C. Haynes, NAACP’s Senior Vice President of Policy and Legislative Affairs. “Every voter should know that the basic information they receive about how to vote and register is accurate. But without action from Congress, information can be as artificial as the so-called intelligence at creates it. With the growth of AI tools powering dis-information, we need to pass the Securing Elections from AI Deception Act so that Black voters are protected and the sources of dis-information are held accountable,” said Chanel Sherrod, Policy Advisor at the Lawyers’ Committee for Civil Rights Under Law . Brown serves at the Ranking Member on the Cybersecurity, Information Technology, and Government Innovation Subcommittee on the House Oversight Committee. Brown first introduced the Securing Elections from AI Deception Act in 2024. Requires Disclaimers on Election-Related Content Generated by Artificial Intelligence

extraction.body: Washington, DC – Congresswoman Shontel Brown (OH-11) has introduced the Securing Elections from AI Deception Act , legislation to prohibit the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to deprive or defraud individuals of their right to vote and require disclaimers on AI-generated content. The legislation would be enforced by the Federal Trade Commission and applies to federal, state, and local campaign content. The Securing Elections from AI Deception Act is endorsed by the NAACP, the Lawyer’s Committee for Civil Rights Under Law, and NETWORK Lobby for Catholic Social Justice. The legislation has 30 cosponsors in the House. Bill text available here . This week, the New York Times reported that over $130 million in AI-generated ads have flooded the airwaves this election year. According to analysis by Wesleyan University, 69% of ads with AI content do not have disclaimers . Campaign ads featuring deceptive AI-generated have proliferated in recent years ( Wall Street Journal , Reuters , New York Times ), including ads featuring deepfake video and audio. In 2024, deepfake images of Trump with Black supporters spread online . In addition to deceiving voters, AI could also be used to spread false information regarding election information as a tactic to suppress voting rights. In 2020, robocalls targeting Black voters in Ohio spread deliberately false information relating to voting by mail procedures. AI technology has the potential to encourage similar efforts in the future and make them more persuasive. “This isn’t complicated: voters deserve to know that the campaign content they see and hear is real. We need labels on AI-generated election content and we need to hold accountable those who use AI to knowingly spread false information. Pairing the latest technology with old-school dirty tricks is a dangerous combination. I’m proud to introduce the Securing Elections from AI Deception Act and will continue to defend the voting rights of every American,” said Congresswoman Shontel Brown . “Artificial intelligence cannot become another tool for voter deception and suppression. Black communities have long been targeted by efforts to mislead, intimidate, and exclude voters, and new technology can make those tactics more sophisticated and harder to detect. The Securing Elections From AI Deception Act puts necessary guardrails in place to protect voters and our democracy. The NAACP applauds Congresswoman Brown for her continued leadership,” said Cedric C. Haynes, NAACP’s Senior Vice President of Policy and Legislative Affairs. “Every voter should know that the basic information they receive about how to vote and register is accurate. But without action from Congress, information can be as artificial as the so-called intelligence at creates it. With the growth of AI tools powering dis-information, we need to pass the Securing Elections from AI Deception Act so that Black voters are protected and the sources of dis-information are held accountable,” said Chanel Sherrod, Policy Advisor at the Lawyers’ Committee for Civil Rights Under Law . Brown serves at the Ranking Member on the Cybersecurity, Information Technology, and Government Innovation Subcommittee on the House Oversight Committee. Brown first introduced the Securing Elections from AI Deception Act in 2024. Requires Disclaimers on Election-Related Content Generated by Artificial Intelligence

extraction.body: Crucial vulnerabilities in a programming language that underpins much of the internet are so severe that European and British authorities have recommended websites temporarily go offline until they can be fixed. The flaws are in PHP, a little-known but crucial programming language which powers how web servers process code. The security team that maintains PHP released patches to fix the problem around 10 a.m. ET. But several websites were temporarily down as of Wednesday morning, citing fear that hackers could take them over. They included Pinboard, a bookmarking site and some parts of Wikipedia . Two massive but largely unmoderated forum sites, 4Chan and Something Awful, both went offline to wait for a patch. Japanese websites were also voluntarily offline, including systems for daycare centers and video games, the Japanese tech news site ITmedia reported . PHP is used in 69% of all websites, according to W3Techs , which surveys the software behind how the internet works. OpenAI said that it helped discover the vulnerability and brought it to PHP’s attention before hackers exploited it more severely. “Given the severity of these flaws and PHP’s widespread use, we consider this one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory,” the company wrote in a blog post Wednesday. “It highlights how AI can uncover security flaws with internet-scale impact, but the same capabilities can also help attackers rapidly develop offensive tools and exploits.” The vulnerability was discovered through OpenAI’s program to give cybersecurity companies access to ChatGPT models that are adept at finding software flaws, the company said. As websites around the world patched the flaws Wednesday, it was unclear how severely hackers were already exploiting it. Patchstack, a cybersecurity platform , said it had received “reports of active exploitation.” The chief technical officer of Cloudflare, one of the internet’s largest website hosting companies, wrote on X, “We are seeing early attacks emerging and are updating mitigations as new vectors show up.” Government agencies around the world, including the U.S. National Security Agency, have warned of the flaws and recommended potentially taking sites offline until they’re fixed. CERT-EU , the European Union’s technical cybersecurity advisory body, said, “Organisations should consider isolating internet-facing applications from public networks until a fix is available.” The United Kingdom’s National Cyber Security Centre recommended, “Where immediate remediation is not feasible, organisations should consider taking the system offline until it can be fully mitigated.” The primary U.S. cybersecurity agency, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, said in an advisory late Wednesday morning that it recommended patching the software flaws, but that it had “not observed exploitation of these vulnerabilities as of the time of publication.”

extraction.body: Justin Mast’s life was changed by a cyborg plant. A few years ago, Mast was reading through some scientific literature when he stumbled upon research about a houseplant wired to a motorized stand . When the plant wanted more light, electrical signals flowed through the living tissues. A control board sensed the current and wheeled the plant closer to the light source. “I’m like, what the heck?” Mast told TechCrunch. “That was the entry to the rabbit hole for me.” Mast wound up partnering with Lee von Kraus, a neuroscientist who has worked with DARPA, to found Electric Plant , which has been spending the past three years collecting data to build a large language model, Bombadil, capable of interpreting the subtle electrical signals coursing through a plant’s stem and relaying details about the plant’s needs to growers. The founders believe their model could one day lead to a tool that would let people “speak” to plants. “We’re listening more than we’re speaking, but listening’s the first step,” said Mast, co-founder and CEO of Electric Plant. To bring its sensors and Bombadil to market, Electric Plant recently raised an $11.2 million seed round led by Onto Ventures and Climactic, with participation from Ponderosa, Endeavor Catalyst, Ludlow, Michigan Rise, The Fund, Schox VC, and Dug Song. Even in the most controlled greenhouses, farmers and growers don’t have full visibility of what their plants require, Mast said. Traditionally, farmers, growers, and foresters have relied on coarse tools that react to plants’ demands for water, nutrients, or light. And tools like soil probes, handheld spectroscopes, and satellite imagery work well enough, but they leave much to be desired, Mast said. “That technology is sophisticated, but its ability to get at the inside of the plant isn’t very sophisticated. Most of that stuff still lags quite a bit behind the real-time needs of the plant,” he said. Electric Plant had to start somewhere, though, so it used those devices to train its Bombadil model, which is capable of interpreting electrical signals in about 125 different species. “We know the model will surpass a lot of that equipment,” Mast said. The startup’s sensors are also significantly cheaper than existing tools, which generally cost thousands of dollars. “This is tens of dollars,” he said. The sensors, about the size of a regular iPhone folded lengthwise, are attached to a plant using stainless steel screws. The screws must penetrate the cambium — the layer of living tissue just under the bark — to connect to the microvolt changes occurring within the plant. Data collected from these sensors is sent to a base station via a low-power wireless network. Electric Plant only needs a couple sensors per acre for accurate results, Mast said. The data gets interpreted by Bombadil in the cloud, and the results are sent back to the customer, who can use it to, for example, adjust their watering or fertilizer schedules. Mast claims such a system can boost yields while reducing water use by 20% or more. Mast wouldn’t disclose who Electric Plant’s initial customers are, but it’s easy to imagine applications in agriculture and forestry. Bombadil’s first hundred-plus species runs the gamut of plant forms, from ferns, redwoods, and tomatoes to dahlias, Mast said. “This is the most diverse model ever created on biological electrical signals,” he said. “No one’s ever done anything equivalent to this in the animal world.” When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . extraction.body: Justin Mast’s life was changed by a cyborg plant. A few years ago, Mast was reading through some scientific literature when he stumbled upon research about a houseplant wired to a motorized stand . When the plant wanted more light, electrical signals flowed through the living tissues. A control board sensed the current and wheeled the plant closer to the light source. “I’m like, what the heck?” Mast told TechCrunch. “That was the entry to the rabbit hole for me.” Mast wound up partnering with Lee von Kraus, a neuroscientist who has worked with DARPA, to found Electric Plant , which has been spending the past three years collecting data to build a large language model, Bombadil, capable of interpreting the subtle electrical signals coursing through a plant’s stem and relaying details about the plant’s needs to growers. The founders believe their model could one day lead to a tool that would let people “speak” to plants. “We’re listening more than we’re speaking, but listening’s the first step,” said Mast, co-founder and CEO of Electric Plant. To bring its sensors and Bombadil to market, Electric Plant recently raised an $11.2 million seed round led by Onto Ventures and Climactic, with participation from Ponderosa, Endeavor Catalyst, Ludlow, Michigan Rise, The Fund, Schox VC, and Dug Song. Even in the most controlled greenhouses, farmers and growers don’t have full visibility of what their plants require, Mast said. Traditionally, farmers, growers, and foresters have relied on coarse tools that react to plants’ demands for water, nutrients, or light. And tools like soil probes, handheld spectroscopes, and satellite imagery work well enough, but they leave much to be desired, Mast said. “That technology is sophisticated, but its ability to get at the inside of the plant isn’t very sophisticated. Most of that stuff still lags quite a bit behind the real-time needs of the plant,” he said. Electric Plant had to start somewhere, though, so it used those devices to train its Bombadil model, which is capable of interpreting electrical signals in about 125 different species. “We know the model will surpass a lot of that equipment,” Mast said. The startup’s sensors are also significantly cheaper than existing tools, which generally cost thousands of dollars. “This is tens of dollars,” he said. The sensors, about the size of a regular iPhone folded lengthwise, are attached to a plant using stainless steel screws. The screws must penetrate the cambium — the layer of living tissue just under the bark — to connect to the microvolt changes occurring within the plant. Data collected from these sensors is sent to a base station via a low-power wireless network. Electric Plant only needs a couple sensors per acre for accurate results, Mast said. The data gets interpreted by Bombadil in the cloud, and the results are sent back to the customer, who can use it to, for example, adjust their watering or fertilizer schedules. Mast claims such a system can boost yields while reducing water use by 20% or more. Mast wouldn’t disclose who Electric Plant’s initial customers are, but it’s easy to imagine applications in agriculture and forestry. Bombadil’s first hundred-plus species runs the gamut of plant forms, from ferns, redwoods, and tomatoes to dahlias, Mast said. “This is the most diverse model ever created on biological electrical signals,” he said. “No one’s ever done anything equivalent to this in the animal world.” When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . PHP rates both CVSS v4.0 9.2 (Critical) . The fixed versions are PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 , released on 21 October 2026. PHP's GitHub security advisories were published at 13:34 UTC (16:34 Cyprus time), ahead of the scheduled 14:00 UTC release time. PHP's security advisory says "all PHP installations serving web requests" are at risk, including PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed. PHP considers the risk "highest for mod_php, with a demonstrated exploit where an unauthenticated request can trigger the attack before any application code runs." PHP says "There are no complete mitigations, updating is the only safe choice." PHP powers many websites and web applications, including content management systems, e-commerce platforms and custom web services (BleepingComputer), so it is very likely to be somewhere in your vendors' stacks. PHP describes the two flaws as follows (php.net security advisory and GitHub advisories): Both have the CVSS v4.0 vector AV:N/AC:H/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N (score 9.2) from PHP as CNA. For CVE-2026-109618, PHP says complete remote code execution "was validated over HTTP against mod_php", and that source analysis supports PHP-FPM as susceptible, "though no complete FPM exploit has been demonstrated". For CVE-2026-109619, PHP says "Session lifecycle RCE was validated against mod_php and FPM"; it adds that the FPM path "depends on a suitable application operation" ( GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp ). This advisory does not cover how to exploit the flaws. PHP's CVE records credit Ryan at Calif.io, Wiz and OpenAI with reporting or finding the flaws, and PHP developers Arnaud Le Blanc, Ilija Tovilo, Jakub Zelenka and Nora Dossche with the fix. PHP, CERT-EU and the NCSC have released no indicators of compromise. Cloudflare says it was seeing early attacks before the release but has not published details. extraction.body: Update (21 Oct 2026): PHP has shipped its security release. PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 fix the two vulnerabilities, which PHP now confirms are CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 . PHP's CNA rates both CVSS v4.0 9.2 (Critical) . Both CVEs are published on cve.org; NVD received both records on 21 October and lists them as "Received", with no NVD score yet (it shows PHP's 9.2). Neither CVE is in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog (catalog version 2026.10.20, released 20 Oct 2026, checked 21 Oct 2026, 17:29 Cyprus time). PHP says "updating is the only safe choice" ( PHP security advisory ). Patch now. PHP has released fixes for two critical vulnerabilities that can allow unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE) on servers that run PHP to serve web requests. PHP rates both CVSS v4.0 9.2 (Critical) . The fixed versions are PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 , released on 21 October 2026. PHP's GitHub security advisories were published at 13:34 UTC (16:34 Cyprus time), ahead of the scheduled 14:00 UTC release time. PHP's security advisory says "all PHP installations serving web requests" are at risk, including PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed. PHP considers the risk "highest for mod_php, with a demonstrated exploit where an unauthenticated request can trigger the attack before any application code runs." PHP says "There are no complete mitigations, updating is the only safe choice." PHP powers many websites and web applications, including content management systems, e-commerce platforms and custom web services (BleepingComputer), so it is very likely to be somewhere in your vendors' stacks. PHP describes the two flaws as follows (php.net security advisory and GitHub advisories): Both have the CVSS v4.0 vector AV:N/AC:H/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N (score 9.2) from PHP as CNA. For CVE-2026-109618, PHP says complete remote code execution "was validated over HTTP against mod_php", and that source analysis supports PHP-FPM as susceptible, "though no complete FPM exploit has been demonstrated". For CVE-2026-109619, PHP says "Session lifecycle RCE was validated against mod_php and FPM"; it adds that the FPM path "depends on a suitable application operation" ( GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp ). This advisory does not cover how to exploit the flaws. PHP's CVE records credit Ryan at Calif.io, Wiz and OpenAI with reporting or finding the flaws, and PHP developers Arnaud Le Blanc, Ilija Tovilo, Jakub Zelenka and Nora Dossche with the fix. CVE / KEV status (checked 21 Oct 2026, 17:29 Cyprus time): Both CVEs are published on cve.org by PHP. NVD lists both as "Received" and shows only PHP's CNA score (CVSS v4.0 9.2, Critical). NVD has not published its own score. Neither CVE is in CISA's KEV catalog (catalog version 2026.10.20, released 20 Oct 2026). None published. PHP, CERT-EU and the NCSC have released no indicators of compromise. Cloudflare says it was seeing early attacks before the release but has not published details. Rescana has not confirmed in-the-wild exploitation, and neither CVE is in CISA's KEV catalog as of this update. The fix is now out, but you are only protected once every vendor running PHP in its stack has deployed it, and many of those dependencies are invisible from the outside. Ask your critical vendors now whether they run PHP, including bundled runtimes and appliances, whether they are on 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, 8.2.35 or a patched vendor build, and when they will finish. Then follow up until each one confirms. What we will update: We will update this post if NVD publishes its own assessment, if either CVE is added to CISA's KEV catalog, or if PHP revises its advisories. extraction.body: Last week was the worst stretch for chip stocks in over a year. The Philadelphia Semiconductor index dropped more than 11%, a hot inflation print raised the cost of funding every data center on the drawing board, and the impact of worries about CoreWeave 's ( CRWV -0.71% ) debt load spread to every company selling into AI infrastructure. Marvell Technology ( MRVL +1.70% ) sank by nearly 17% in five days. And yet, if your goal is to own one AI chip stock heading into 2027, that decline is the reason why you should look into picking up shares of Marvell now rather than later. Even as investors were selling, the company spent the week revealing its most specific, product-level work of the year, and almost nobody noticed because they were watching the tape. Marvell is not a GPU company. It designs chips that sit around GPUs: the custom accelerators that hyperscalers and AI labs are building for their specific workloads, the optical and copper links that connect thousands of processors into clusters, and the memory controllers that keep those chips fed with data. That is the business the company put on display at the Open Compute Project Global Summit in San Jose from Oct. 12 to Oct. 15. Two announcements from the event stood out to me. On Oct. 12, Marvell unveiled the second generation of its Structera X memory expanders -- chips built to attack what the company calls the "memory wall" in AI inference. The problem is simple: As models get bigger and context windows get longer, GPUs run out of memory before they run out of math. Structera X lets a server bolt on up to 6 terabytes of standard DDR5 memory, share it across four hosts, and compress it on the fly, which the company says cuts time to first token by 40% to 50%. The first generation Structera X is already shipping to hyperscalers, and a Meta Platforms ( META +2.38% ) hardware engineering director was quoted in the company's release. Test models of the second generation will be available in Q1 2027. Then, on Oct. 13, Marvell followed by unveiling two 3-nanometer connectivity chips, a 3.2-terabit retimer and a new active electrical cable chip that doubles copper reach to more than six meters between AI servers and switches. Both support UALink, the open standard that non-Nvidia accelerators use to talk to each other. Early samples of both are already available for potential customers. That sounds like a lot of jargon, so here is the plain version. An AI processor's usefulness will always be limited by the memory it can reach and the capacity of the connections that link it to neighboring chips. The new products Marvell announced last week address both of those bottlenecks: one lets a server strap on far more memory than the GPU came with, so it can handle bigger models without choking, and the other helps racks of accelerators talk to each other over longer, cheaper copper cables without the signal falling apart. These are tools crucial for AI infrastructure, and Marvell is selling them. On Oct. 6 -- a week before the AI sector rout -- Marvell held its first investor day in years , and management used the event to publicize a target worth reading twice: It's aiming for revenue in the range of $70 billion to $90 billion by its fiscal 2031, up from $8.2 billion in fiscal 2026, with implied non-GAAP earnings above $30 per share . The engine driving it toward those targets is what management calls "XPU attach," the networking, memory, and security chips that get pulled along with every custom accelerator a cloud provider designs. Big targets deserve some skepticism, and this one assumes 55% to 60% annualized growth for five years. But even if it achieves growth at half that rate, the stock near $228 is cheap against what the company expects to earn. Nvidia ( NVDA +1.81% ) saw enough to buy $2 billion of Marvell preferred stock in March, and Nvidia does not make such investments casually. But last week's sell-off was driven by financing fears, not by any customers walking away, and Marvell kept shipping through it. For anyone able to buy this stock and hold onto it through 2027 or longer, the 17% discount the market just gave it makes it look like a steal. passages: At the very start of its analysis, ChatGPT took into consideration the likely major development in store for Ripple and $XRP in 2024.
The AI focused, in particular, on the effect the resolution of the SEC lawsuit might have.
It also stated that Bitcoin (BTC) halving is likely to have a significant impact – no matter what else happens in the crypto market.

With the recent rallies and accompanying enthusiasm for a strong 2024, and the ever-present dangers in mind, Finbold consulted ChatGPT – the flagship artificial intelligence (AI) platform of OpenAI – on January 2, 2024, on how $XRP might fare throughout the year.

Interestingly, the artificial intelligence does not foresee the cryptocurrency ending 2024 at its yearly highs.
It also predicted that, should no calamity occur, the Bitcoin halving alone could potentially send $XRP as high as $4.

For example, a major bull market paired with a decisive legal victory could see $XRP close to $5 on December 31, 2024, while its conservative scenario – one of significant market volatility and persisting legal troubles – places it no higher than $1.
Still, challenges for $XRP persist, as was reflected by the fact that it, despite several significant surges, failed to maintain a decisive upward momentum.
Its victory against the SEC isn’t guaranteed, and while 2024 appears like it will bring a bull market for crypto, it is unclear if it will truly be smooth sailing in the coming months.
ChatGPT also offered two additional scenarios that assume more conservative developments.
Still, this does not truly indicate that a victory is certain; rather, most experts, pundits, and commentators are currently estimating a favorable outcome for Brad Garlinghouse’s company.

This was driven by broader market conditions, a string of legal victories in its long-standing struggle with the SEC, and Ripple’s continued expansion of central bank digital currency (CBDC) partnerships.

In addition to institutional demand, Interest rates remain another important factor when it comes to Bitcoin price prediction 2026.

extraction.body: PHP shipped emergency patches for two critical PHP2Shell flaws that allow unauthenticated code execution. The twist: researchers found them with OpenAI and Google AI models, days before the fix was due. PHP shipped emergency security updates on Wednesday. They fix two critical flaws that let an unauthenticated attacker run code on almost any server running the language. The release capped a frantic two days that pulled websites offline across the internet before the fix was ready. The patched releases are PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35. They fix two memory-safety bugs, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, each rated 9.2 on the CVSS v4 scale, PHP said in its advisory. The project called updating “the only safe choice”. It said the risk is highest for sites running Apache with mod_php, where an unauthenticated request can trigger the flaw before any application code runs. What makes the release unusual is how the bugs surfaced. Security firm Calif found the first one in August, with help from OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol model. It came during an audit of PHP’s source code that OpenAI funded through its Patch the Planet initiative. Google’s Wiz team said it found the flaws independently, weeks later. It used Wiz Atlas, Google’s Gemini 4 Argon and GPT-5.6 Sol. PHP’s advisory credits researchers from Calif, Wiz and OpenAI together. OpenAI framed the find as proof that AI can catch internet-scale flaws before criminals do. It calls this a Defender’s Window. “Given the severity of these flaws and PHP’s widespread use, we consider this one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory,” OpenAI wrote. The company has committed $1bn in subsidised access to its Daybreak cyber programme for under-resourced defenders. Calif struck a more measured note. In its own write-up , the firm said it used only generally available models and no special tooling. Knowing PHP’s history, it said, mattered more than the model. “No model is simply capable of unearthing ‘all bugs’ with simple prompts. At least for now,” the company wrote. OpenAI models helped researchers discover critical security flaws in PHP. Governments and companies did not wait. The EU’s cyber agency CERT-EU and Britain’s NCSC both advised organisations to take systems offline where they could not patch at once. The US National Security Agency issued its own alert. The bookmarking service Pinboard, the GrapheneOS forum and the streaming tool OBS pulled parts of their sites down. Laravel halted its Cloud deployments while it rebuilt on patched images. The release also came early. PHP had scheduled it for 14:00 UTC, with a wider embargo due to lift the next day. It brought the fix forward after details leaked in a post to Hacker News, the Wall Street Journal reported. Security firm watchTowr confirmed the bugs were real before any patch existed. A proof-of-concept exploit then circulated online. Volker Dusch, a security engineer at the nonprofit PHP Foundation, told the Wall Street Journal it was the most severe issue PHP had faced in more than a decade. He likened it to Heartbleed, the 2014 bug that forced a global patching race. Wiz compared the flaws to both Heartbleed and Log4Shell. It estimates PHP runs roughly 70% of all websites. PHP did not name the oldest affected version. But Calif, Wiz and Cloudflare all put the reach at PHP 5.4 and later, more than a decade of releases. PHP’s team published backported fixes for the unsupported 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1 branches, given the severity. It warned that no configuration change is a complete substitute for updating. WordPress, which runs on PHP, urged site owners to update. It noted that versions before 8.2 no longer receive security fixes. Infrastructure providers moved to blunt attacks in the gap. Cloudflare said it switched on web application firewall rules for every customer, free accounts included, at 03:02 UTC. That was about nine hours before disclosure, the company said. It watched attackers mutate their payloads against the rules as they landed. PHP changes are live. Start patching. Huge thanks to coordinated work by @ThePHPF! This is the second time in months that AI-found flaws in web software have forced a mass update. The mass-exploited WordPress bugs came in July. OpenAI said the PHP flaws are among several serious vulnerabilities it has already found. It expects “similar findings to increase sharply” in the coming months. For now, the only fix PHP endorses is the update itself. extraction.body: This story is developing and was written before PHP's scheduled 14:00 UTC release on October 21. Once the release is out, the affected and fixed versions below are confirmed by the official advisory. PHP will ship an out-of-cycle security release at 14:00 UTC today, October 21, for two critical vulnerabilities that its security team has rated 9.2 on the CVSS v4.0 scale but has not described. ⚡ UPDATE — PHP Issues Emergency Patches for Two Critical PHP2Shell RCE Flaws as Exploit Attempts Emerge Security researchers at watchTowr say the two flaws allow remote code execution. Only the four supported PHP branches, 8.2 through 8.5, can receive the fix, and no exploitation has been reported so far. The advance notice followed a leak. On October 20, a post on HN said two PHP remote code execution flaws, rated CVSS 10.0 and affecting versions from PHP 5 onward, would be disclosed on Thursday, October 22. The poster said they had "no evidence beyond 'source: trust me, bro'". watchTowr then posted on X that the leaked information was real, that the two flaws were under embargo, that everyone had been supposed to wait until Thursday, and that it could not share more for now. PHP published its notice that evening, at 19:33 UTC, with the release set for Wednesday, a day before the date watchTowr gave. The notice says PHP may release earlier "should details of either vulnerability become public, or should evidence of active exploitation appear in the wild." The leak carried the flaws' existence, a score, a date, and two CVE identifiers, not how the flaws work. The CVSS 10.0 figure is the leak's. PHP's rating is 9.2 on version 4.0 of the scale. The identifiers researchers are using, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 , were also listed in the leaked post. PHP's notice names neither. The claim that every version since PHP 5 is affected is unconfirmed too: watchTowr's own FAQ on the flaws says that scope "has not been confirmed by an official vendor advisory" and that no configuration or feature requirement has been described. PHP says "Full details, affected versions, and the fixed versions will be published with the release." Researchers have started calling the pair php2shell. The name is theirs, not PHP's. Whatever the affected range turns out to be, PHP issues fixes only for its four supported branches , and records each branch's changes in its changelog . Versions 8.2 and 8.3 receive only security fixes, and 8.4 and 8.5 are in active support. Ahead of the release, several trackers, including Alpine Linux's and security researcher Kevin Beaumont, expect the fixes to ship as PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35, the next point release of each branch, though PHP has not confirmed the numbers. Anything older, including 8.1, 8.0, 7.x, and 5.x, is end of life and gets no PHP fix. If the flaws reach those branches, installations on them will have no vendor patch. Security company Mallory counted about 884,000 internet-facing hosts whose HTTP banner reported a PHP version of 8.1 or older to the Shodan search engine on October 20, 59% of the roughly 1.5 million hosts that reported any version. The count covers banners, not confirmed affected systems, and a further 740,000 hosts reported PHP without a version. PHP has published no workaround. Until the release lands, the preparation comes down to six steps, most of them drawn from a rapid-response post from Huntress , with CERT-EU's isolation advice added. Huntress said it had not seen exploitation of the flaws in its partner environments as of October 20, had not built or reproduced a proof of concept, and was not aware of public exploit code. watchTowr's FAQ lists exploitation as none reported as of October 21 and the flaws as not in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. For comparison, when CVE-2024-4577 , a PHP flaw in CGI mode on Windows, became public in June 2024, Akamai saw exploit attempts against its honeypot servers within 24 hours. The release should clarify what the notice withheld: which versions are affected, which part of PHP is involved, whether an attack requires a particular way of running PHP, a configuration, or a login, and how PHP itself describes the flaws. At the time of writing, PHP had not released the fixes. extraction.body: PHP shipped emergency patches for two critical PHP2Shell flaws that allow unauthenticated code execution. The twist: researchers found them with OpenAI and Google AI models, days before the fix was due. PHP shipped emergency security updates on Wednesday. They fix two critical flaws that let an unauthenticated attacker run code on almost any server running the language. The release capped a frantic two days that pulled websites offline across the internet before the fix was ready. The patched releases are PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35. They fix two memory-safety bugs, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, each rated 9.2 on the CVSS v4 scale, PHP said in its advisory. The project called updating “the only safe choice”. It said the risk is highest for sites running Apache with mod_php, where an unauthenticated request can trigger the flaw before any application code runs. What makes the release unusual is how the bugs surfaced. Security firm Calif found the first one in August, with help from OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol model. It came during an audit of PHP’s source code that OpenAI funded through its Patch the Planet initiative. Google’s Wiz team said it found the flaws independently, weeks later. It used Wiz Atlas, Google’s Gemini 4 Argon and GPT-5.6 Sol. PHP’s advisory credits researchers from Calif, Wiz and OpenAI together. OpenAI framed the find as proof that AI can catch internet-scale flaws before criminals do. It calls this a Defender’s Window. “Given the severity of these flaws and PHP’s widespread use, we consider this one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory,” OpenAI wrote. The company has committed $1bn in subsidised access to its Daybreak cyber programme for under-resourced defenders. Calif struck a more measured note. In its own write-up , the firm said it used only generally available models and no special tooling. Knowing PHP’s history, it said, mattered more than the model. “No model is simply capable of unearthing ‘all bugs’ with simple prompts. At least for now,” the company wrote. OpenAI models helped researchers discover critical security flaws in PHP. Governments and companies did not wait. The EU’s cyber agency CERT-EU and Britain’s NCSC both advised organisations to take systems offline where they could not patch at once. The US National Security Agency issued its own alert. The bookmarking service Pinboard, the GrapheneOS forum and the streaming tool OBS pulled parts of their sites down. Laravel halted its Cloud deployments while it rebuilt on patched images. The release also came early. PHP had scheduled it for 14:00 UTC, with a wider embargo due to lift the next day. It brought the fix forward after details leaked in a post to Hacker News, the Wall Street Journal reported. Security firm watchTowr confirmed the bugs were real before any patch existed. A proof-of-concept exploit then circulated online. Volker Dusch, a security engineer at the nonprofit PHP Foundation, told the Wall Street Journal it was the most severe issue PHP had faced in more than a decade. He likened it to Heartbleed, the 2014 bug that forced a global patching race. Wiz compared the flaws to both Heartbleed and Log4Shell. It estimates PHP runs roughly 70% of all websites. PHP did not name the oldest affected version. But Calif, Wiz and Cloudflare all put the reach at PHP 5.4 and later, more than a decade of releases. PHP’s team published backported fixes for the unsupported 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1 branches, given the severity. It warned that no configuration change is a complete substitute for updating. WordPress, which runs on PHP, urged site owners to update. It noted that versions before 8.2 no longer receive security fixes. Infrastructure providers moved to blunt attacks in the gap. Cloudflare said it switched on web application firewall rules for every customer, free accounts included, at 03:02 UTC. That was about nine hours before disclosure, the company said. It watched attackers mutate their payloads against the rules as they landed. PHP changes are live. Start patching. Huge thanks to coordinated work by @ThePHPF! This is the second time in months that AI-found flaws in web software have forced a mass update. The mass-exploited WordPress bugs came in July. OpenAI said the PHP flaws are among several serious vulnerabilities it has already found. It expects “similar findings to increase sharply” in the coming months. For now, the only fix PHP endorses is the update itself. PHP shipped emergency security updates on Wednesday. They fix two critical flaws that let an unauthenticated attacker run code on almost any server running the language. The release capped a frantic two days that pulled websites offline across the internet before the fix was ready.

The patched releases are PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35. They fix two memory-safety bugs, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, each rated 9.2 on the CVSS v4 scale, PHP said in its advisory. The project called updating “the only safe choice”. It said the risk is highest for sites running Apache with mod_php, where an unauthenticated request can trigger the flaw before any application code runs.

What makes the release unusual is how the bugs surfaced. Security firm Calif found the first one in August, with help from OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol model. It came during an audit of PHP’s source code that OpenAI funded through its Patch the Planet initiative. Google’s Wiz team said it found the flaws independently, weeks later. It used Wiz Atlas, Google’s Gemini 4 Argon and GPT-5.6 Sol. PHP’s advisory credits researchers from Calif, Wiz and OpenAI together.
OpenAI framed the find as proof that AI can catch internet-scale flaws before criminals do. It calls this a Defender’s Window.
“Given the severity of these flaws and PHP’s widespread use, we consider this one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory,” OpenAI wrote.

The company has committed $1bn in subsidised access to its Daybreak cyber programme for under-resourced defenders. Calif struck a more measured note. In its own write-up , the firm said it used only generally available models and no special tooling. Knowing PHP’s history, it said, mattered more than the model.
“No model is simply capable of unearthing ‘all bugs’ with simple prompts. At least for now,” the company wrote.
OpenAI models helped researchers discover critical security flaws in PHP.

Governments and companies did not wait. The EU’s cyber agency CERT-EU and Britain’s NCSC both advised organisations to take systems offline where they could not patch at once. The US National Security Agency issued its own alert. The bookmarking service Pinboard, the GrapheneOS forum and the streaming tool OBS pulled parts of their sites down. Laravel halted its Cloud deployments while it rebuilt on patched images.

The release also came early. PHP had scheduled it for 14:00 UTC, with a wider embargo due to lift the next day. It brought the fix forward after details leaked in a post to Hacker News, the Wall Street Journal reported. Security firm watchTowr confirmed the bugs were real before any patch existed. A proof-of-concept exploit then circulated online.

Volker Dusch, a security engineer at the nonprofit PHP Foundation, told the Wall Street Journal it was the most severe issue PHP had faced in more than a decade. He likened it to Heartbleed, the 2014 bug that forced a global patching race. Wiz compared the flaws to both Heartbleed and Log4Shell. It estimates PHP runs roughly 70% of all websites.

PHP did not name the oldest affected version. But Calif, Wiz and Cloudflare all put the reach at PHP 5.4 and later, more than a decade of releases. PHP’s team published backported fixes for the unsupported 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1 branches, given the severity. It warned that no configuration change is a complete substitute for updating. WordPress, which runs on PHP, urged site owners to update. It noted that versions before 8.2 no longer receive security fixes.

Infrastructure providers moved to blunt attacks in the gap. Cloudflare said it switched on web application firewall rules for every customer, free accounts included, at 03:02 UTC. That was about nine hours before disclosure, the company said. It watched attackers mutate their payloads against the rules as they landed.
PHP changes are live. Start patching. Huge thanks to coordinated work by @ThePHPF!

This is the second time in months that AI-found flaws in web software have forced a mass update. The mass-exploited WordPress bugs came in July. OpenAI said the PHP flaws are among several serious vulnerabilities it has already found. It expects “similar findings to increase sharply” in the coming months. For now, the only fix PHP endorses is the update itself.

extraction.body: This story is developing and was written before PHP's scheduled 14:00 UTC release on October 21. Once the release is out, the affected and fixed versions below are confirmed by the official advisory. PHP will ship an out-of-cycle security release at 14:00 UTC today, October 21, for two critical vulnerabilities that its security team has rated 9.2 on the CVSS v4.0 scale but has not described. ⚡ UPDATE — PHP Issues Emergency Patches for Two Critical PHP2Shell RCE Flaws as Exploit Attempts Emerge Security researchers at watchTowr say the two flaws allow remote code execution. Only the four supported PHP branches, 8.2 through 8.5, can receive the fix, and no exploitation has been reported so far. The advance notice followed a leak. On October 20, a post on HN said two PHP remote code execution flaws, rated CVSS 10.0 and affecting versions from PHP 5 onward, would be disclosed on Thursday, October 22. The poster said they had "no evidence beyond 'source: trust me, bro'". watchTowr then posted on X that the leaked information was real, that the two flaws were under embargo, that everyone had been supposed to wait until Thursday, and that it could not share more for now. PHP published its notice that evening, at 19:33 UTC, with the release set for Wednesday, a day before the date watchTowr gave. The notice says PHP may release earlier "should details of either vulnerability become public, or should evidence of active exploitation appear in the wild." The leak carried the flaws' existence, a score, a date, and two CVE identifiers, not how the flaws work. The CVSS 10.0 figure is the leak's. PHP's rating is 9.2 on version 4.0 of the scale. The identifiers researchers are using, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 , were also listed in the leaked post. PHP's notice names neither. The claim that every version since PHP 5 is affected is unconfirmed too: watchTowr's own FAQ on the flaws says that scope "has not been confirmed by an official vendor advisory" and that no configuration or feature requirement has been described. PHP says "Full details, affected versions, and the fixed versions will be published with the release." Researchers have started calling the pair php2shell. The name is theirs, not PHP's. Whatever the affected range turns out to be, PHP issues fixes only for its four supported branches , and records each branch's changes in its changelog . Versions 8.2 and 8.3 receive only security fixes, and 8.4 and 8.5 are in active support. Ahead of the release, several trackers, including Alpine Linux's and security researcher Kevin Beaumont, expect the fixes to ship as PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35, the next point release of each branch, though PHP has not confirmed the numbers. Anything older, including 8.1, 8.0, 7.x, and 5.x, is end of life and gets no PHP fix. If the flaws reach those branches, installations on them will have no vendor patch. Security company Mallory counted about 884,000 internet-facing hosts whose HTTP banner reported a PHP version of 8.1 or older to the Shodan search engine on October 20, 59% of the roughly 1.5 million hosts that reported any version. The count covers banners, not confirmed affected systems, and a further 740,000 hosts reported PHP without a version. PHP has published no workaround. Until the release lands, the preparation comes down to six steps, most of them drawn from a rapid-response post from Huntress , with CERT-EU's isolation advice added. Huntress said it had not seen exploitation of the flaws in its partner environments as of October 20, had not built or reproduced a proof of concept, and was not aware of public exploit code. watchTowr's FAQ lists exploitation as none reported as of October 21 and the flaws as not in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. For comparison, when CVE-2024-4577 , a PHP flaw in CGI mode on Windows, became public in June 2024, Akamai saw exploit attempts against its honeypot servers within 24 hours. The release should clarify what the notice withheld: which versions are affected, which part of PHP is involved, whether an attack requires a particular way of running PHP, a configuration, or a login, and how PHP itself describes the flaws. At the time of writing, PHP had not released the fixes.
